# Architecture Internals (/docs/advanced/architecture-internals)



# Architecture Internals [#architecture-internals]

```
Your app (src/app/**, src/ui/**)
  └── @kwiva/* (public API surface, frozen)
        ├── engines (kysely, elysia, better-auth, devalue, marked, croner, ioredis, files-sdk, nodemailer, resend, pg-boss, @modelcontextprotocol/server, evlog, keyv)
        └── CLI (oxlint + build.ts + tsc)
```

## Boundary rules [#boundary-rules]

1. App code imports only `@kwiva/*`.
2. Engines are sealed (`no-engine-imports` lint gate, oxlint).
3. All public symbols are re-exported via barrels (`src/index.ts`).

## Package dependency graph (from research/dependency-inventory.md) [#package-dependency-graph-from-researchdependency-inventorymd]

| Package   | Depends on                                             |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `http`    | core, data, events, elysia, valibot                    |
| `ui`      | core, http, devalue                                    |
| `client`  | core, http, @tanstack/react-query, @elysia/eden        |
| `auth`    | core, http                                             |
| `jobs`    | core, croner                                           |
| `events`  | core                                                   |
| `mail`    | core, marked                                           |
| `mcp`     | auth, core, data, http                                 |
| `search`  | core, data                                             |
| `storage` | core, files-sdk                                        |
| `testing` | auth, client, core, data, events, http, jobs, mail, ui |
| `cli`     | all                                                    |

> \[!TIP]
> See [Package Boundaries](/docs/advanced/package-boundaries).

# Model IR (/docs/advanced/model-ir)



# Model IR [#model-ir]

## IR structure (frozen) [#ir-structure-frozen]

```ts
ModelDefinition{
  irVersion: 1,
  fields: Record<string, FieldDefinition>,
  relations: Record<string, RelationDefinition>,
  indexes: IndexDefinition[],
  options: ModelOptions,
  hooks: HookDefinition[],
  scopes: ScopeDefinition[],
}
```

Fields: `{name, column, kind, nullable, hasDefault, default?, unique, indexed, primaryKey, enumValues?, description?}`
Relations: `{name, type, target, nullable, through?, foreignKey?, localKey?, onDelete?, morphName?...}`

## Derivation pipeline [#derivation-pipeline]

`defineModel` → `compileIR` → stored in `.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts` + DB artifacts.

## No-drift guarantee [#no-drift-guarantee]

* Types and database never drift: model = source of truth
* `kwiva migrate` diffs schema against IR
* Client typed by route tree

## .kwiva artifacts [#kwiva-artifacts]

* `src/.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts` — typed client/nav
* `src/.kwiva/entry.client.tsx` — browser entry
* `dist/` — built app

> \[!TIP]
> See [Architecture Internals](/docs/advanced/architecture-internals).


# Package Boundaries (/docs/advanced/package-boundaries)



# Package Boundaries [#package-boundaries]

## Graph [#graph]

```
core ──► (all packages depend on it)
├── http → {core, data, events}
├── ui   → {core, http}
├── client → {core, http}
├── auth → {core, http}
├── jobs → {core}
├── events → {core}
├── mail → {core}
├── search → {core, data}
├── storage → {core}
└── testing → {auth, client, core, data, events, http, jobs, mail, ui}
```

## Sealed engines [#sealed-engines]

* `kysely`, `elysia`, `marked`, `better-auth`, `devalue`, `croner`, `ioredis`, `files-sdk`, `nodemailer`, `resend`, `pg-boss`, `@modelcontextprotocol/server`, `evlog`, `keyv`, `@valibot/to-json-schema`, `@elysia/openapi`

See research/dependency-inventory.md.

## Enforcement [#enforcement]

* `test/functionality/engine-imports.test.ts`
* oxlint `no-engine-imports` gate

> \[!TIP]
> App code: only `@kwiva/*`. Engines: framework only.


# Performance (/docs/advanced/performance)



# Performance [#performance]

## Runtime [#runtime]

* **Bun** — fast startup, isolated modules
* **Node** — compatible target

## SSR [#ssr]

* Streaming SSR (Suspense-based, see [Streaming SSR](/docs/rendering/streaming))

## Caching (layered) [#caching-layered]

1. **Route rules** — `ctx.response.set({cache, swr})`
2. **Model cache** — `@kwiva/core` `Cache`
3. **Client cache** — TanStack Query persistence

## Type-level inference [#type-level-inference]

Full type flow from model → route tree → client, zero runtime codegen.

## Startup [#startup]

Kwiva dev is fast (Rust-speed, oxc); Bun runtime.

## Tips [#tips]

* Use `cache.wrap` for expensive operations
* `useUpload` with presigned URLs for large files


# Request Lifecycle (/docs/advanced/request-lifecycle)



# Request Lifecycle (Advanced) [#request-lifecycle-advanced]

See [HTTP Request Lifecycle](/docs/http/lifecycle) for the simplified view.

## Detailed sequence [#detailed-sequence]

1. Elysia server → dispatcher
2. `buildCtx` — parse cookies/params/query/body
3. `validateInput` — Standard Schema, field-mapped errors
4. `compileBeforeHandle` — middleware stack (global→group→route)
5. `wrapHandler` — handler, produce result
6. `validateOutput` — output schema
7. `compileAfterHandle`
8. Error mapping (`toErrorResponse`)
9. Response (optional `waitUntil`, streaming)

## Context propagation [#context-propagation]

`runWithRequest`/`runWithAuth`/`runWithTenant` around handler execution.

## Hooks [#hooks]

* Middleware preflight/main
* Controller hooks (`beforeHandle`, `afterHandle`)
* Route-level `input`/`output` validation

## Timing [#timing]

Auto via logger `ctx.logger` (correlation IDs + durations).


# Agent Integration (/docs/ai-mcp/agent-integration)



# Agent Integration [#agent-integration]

## Enforcement [#enforcement]

Tool calls pass through `executeToolCall` — rate limit → input validation → ability check (`can(policy, user, action, resource)`) → tenant guard (`requireTenant`) → handler → audit log.

## Errors [#errors]

`toolError(code, message?, fields?)` — tools return errors as results; invalid → 400 VALIDATION with fields.

## Audit [#audit]

Every tool call logs: `{tool, name, input, user, tenantId, durationMs, status}` via core logger.

> \[!TIP]
> Use `@kwiva/auth` policies (`ability: "todos.read"`) — same registry as routes.


# AI & MCP (/docs/ai-mcp)



# AI & MCP [#ai--mcp]

Kwiva ships an MCP v2 server (`@kwiva/mcp`) with generated tools derived from models and controllers.

## Entry points [#entry-points]

| Topic             | Page                                                |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| MCP Server        | [MCP Server](/docs/ai-mcp/mcp-server)               |
| Tool Generation   | [Tool Generation](/docs/ai-mcp/tool-generation)     |
| Agent Integration | [Agent Integration](/docs/ai-mcp/agent-integration) |


# MCP Server (/docs/ai-mcp/mcp-server)



# MCP Server [#mcp-server]

## Config (`src/config/mcp.ts`) [#config-srcconfigmcpts]

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  enabled: true,
  route: "/mcp",           // default
  transport: "streamable", // or "stdio"
  auth: "session",         // or "bearer" | "none" (none only with stdio)
  models: ["Todo"],        // model names to expose
  controllers: ["TodosController"], // controller names
  readOnly: false,
  scopes: [],
  requireTenant: false,
});
```

## Enabling [#enabling]

* `enabled: true` in `src/config/mcp.ts`
* CLI: `kwiva mcp` (stdio) and `kwiva mcp:print-config`

## Transports [#transports]

| Transport              | Notes                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `streamable` (default) | HTTP-based, served at `route` on your app server (port 3000 by default) |
| `stdio`                | stdio for local agents; requires `auth: "none"`                         |

## Auth [#auth]

* `session` — session cookie via `requireAuth` on route
* `bearer` — Bearer token (`parseBearer`; uses `@kwiva/auth` API tokens)
* `none` — stdio only

## Client config [#client-config]

`kwiva mcp:print-config` prints:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kwiva": {
      "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp",
      "headers": { "authorization": "Bearer $KWIVA_MCP_TOKEN" } // bearer mode
    }
  }
}
```

For stdio: `{ "command": "kwiva", "args": ["mcp"] }`.

## Connection test [#connection-test]

From Claude Desktop/Cursor/VS Code — add server; restart the client.

> \[!TIP]
> `doctor` checks MCP config: `kwiva doctor`.


# Tool Generation (/docs/ai-mcp/tool-generation)



# Tool Generation [#tool-generation]

## Model tools [#model-tools]

`generateModelTools({config, models?, executor?})` → `McpTool[]`:

| Tool name      | Action | Notes                 |
| -------------- | ------ | --------------------- |
| `todos_list`   | list   | GET /api/todos        |
| `todos_create` | create | POST /api/todos       |
| `todos_get`    | get    | GET /api/todos/:id    |
| `todos_update` | update | PATCH /api/todos/:id  |
| `todos_delete` | delete | DELETE /api/todos/:id |

With `readOnly: true` — only list/get.

## Controller tools [#controller-tools]

`generateControllerTools({config, manifest?, executor?})` → per non-WS route: `TodosController_create` etc.

## Custom tools [#custom-tools]

```ts title="src/app/mcp/tools/audit.ts"
import { defineMcpTool } from "@kwiva/mcp";

export const AuditTool = defineMcpTool({
  description: "Dump current state to audit log",
  input: { table: { type: "string" } },
  ability: "audit.read", // policy check via can(...)
  handler: async ({ input }) => { return { content: [{ type: "text", text: `audit ${input.table}` }] }; },
});
```

## Schema generation [#schema-generation]

* `inputToJsonSchema(input)` — JSON Schema from Standard Schema or field map
* `MCP_TOOL_SUFFIX = "Tool"` — naming convention
* `registerMcpTool(name, tool)` — adds suffix, returns `McpTool`

> \[!TIP]
> Custom tools are discovered via `src/app/mcp/tools/**` recursive scan.


# API Authentication (/docs/api/authentication)



# API Authentication [#api-authentication]

## Surface [#surface]

* `POST /auth/login` — `{email, password}` → cookie + session
* `POST /auth/register`
* `GET /session` — reads cookie
* `GET /auth/logout` (with requireAuth)

## Middleware [#middleware]

`requireAuth({secret?, maxAge?, cookie?, store?, users?})` — attaches `ctx.session/ctx.user/ctx.can`.
`apiTokenAuth({header?, can?})` — Bearer tokens (`parseBearer`, `authorizeHeader`).
`verified()` — 403 unless email verified.
`passwordConfirmation()` — double-submit.

## Sessions [#sessions]

HMAC-signed cookies; `Session{id, userId, expiresAt, remember?}`.

## Enumeration safety [#enumeration-safety]

401 `UNAUTHORIZED` for missing, 403 `FORBIDDEN` for unauthorized — same as unknown.

## Client [#client]

`useSession(endpoint="/session")` — returns `{session, user, isLoading, refresh}`.

## Rate limiting (built-in) [#rate-limiting-built-in]

Login rate limit: `DEFAULT_LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT{max:5, windowMs:60000}` — per-`5/60s` per key (`login:ip:email`).

> \[!TIP]
> For MFA, PKCE OAuth, magic links: see [Auth Providers](/docs/auth/providers).


# Client SDK (/docs/api/client)



# Client SDK [#client-sdk]

Typed client (Eden + TanStack Query).

## Config [#config]

```ts title="src/config/client.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  baseUrl: "https://api.example.com",
  credentials: "include",
  headers: { "x-app": "kwiva" },
  websocket: { url: "wss://api.example.com/ws" },
});
```

## Singleton [#singleton]

| Symbol                                      | Signature                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `client`                                    | Proxy — `client.Todos.list()`                        |
| `initClient(config)`                        | → `TypedClient`                                      |
| `resetClient()`                             | —                                                    |
| `getClientSnapshot()`                       | → `{baseUrl, wsUrl, routes, reconnect}`              |
| `callRoute(routeId, args?, opts?)`          | → `Promise<unknown>`                                 |
| `toClientError(status, value)`              | → `ClientErrorShape{code, message, status, fields?}` |
| `substitutePath(template, params, routeId)` | → segments                                           |

## Data hooks [#data-hooks]

| Hook                                        | Signature                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `useResource(routeId, args?, options?)`     | TanStack Query wrapper                                               |
| `useList(routeId, args?, options?)`         | —                                                                    |
| `useMutation(routeId, options?)`            | → `{mutateAsync, routeFamily, invalidate}`                           |
| `useUpload(routeId, options?)`              | multipart mutations                                                  |
| `useInfiniteList(routeId, args?, options?)` | → `{items, loadNext, hasNext}`                                       |
| `useForm(initial, options?)`                | `{data, setData, errors, processing, submit, post/patch/put/delete}` |
| `routeKey(routeId, args?)`                  | → `["kwiva", controller, method, args?]`                             |

## Cache persistence [#cache-persistence]

`enableCachePersistence({storage, maxAge, throttleMs})` → disposer; `clearPersistedCache()`.

## Token refresh [#token-refresh]

`createTokenRefreshFetch(options)` — retries once on 401.

## WS hooks [#ws-hooks]

`connectRoute(routeId, args?, {reconnect?})`, `useWsSubscription`, `useConnectionState`.

> \[!TIP]
> Built on `@elysia/eden` (Eden) + `@tanstack/react-query`.


# API Errors (/docs/api/errors)



# API Errors [#api-errors]

## Taxonomy [#taxonomy]

8 codes: `BAD_REQUEST`, `UNAUTHORIZED`, `FORBIDDEN`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `VALIDATION`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `INTERNAL` + storage/search codes. See [Errors](/docs/http/errors).

## Envelope [#envelope]

```json
{ "error": { "code", "message", "fields"?, "requestId" } }
```

## Validation [#validation]

422 `VALIDATION` with `fields: Record<string, string[]>`.

## Typed client [#typed-client]

`toClientError(status, value)` → `ClientErrorShape{code, message, status, fields?, requestId?}`.

## Storage/Search codes [#storagesearch-codes]

`STORAGE_NOT_FOUND`, `STORAGE_TENANT_REQUIRED`, `SEARCH_NOT_CONFIGURED` — see [@kwiva/storage](/api/storage), [@kwiva/search](/api/search).

> \[!TIP]
> All errors include `requestId` for tracing.


# Generated Endpoints (/docs/api/generated-endpoints)



# Generated Endpoints [#generated-endpoints]

`defineModel` → 5 REST routes via `restRoutes(model)` → `restBasePath(name)`.

| Method    | Path               | Description                              |
| --------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| GET       | `/api/{model}`     | List (validated where/page/orderBy/with) |
| POST      | `/api/{model}`     | Create                                   |
| GET       | `/api/{model}/:id` | Get                                      |
| PATCH/PUT | `/api/{model}/:id` | Update                                   |
| DELETE    | `/api/{model}/:id` | Remove                                   |

## Contracts [#contracts]

Auto-generated per route; `ctx.input.body` typed via `InputOf<Model>`.

## Permissions [#permissions]

`model.options.permission` + `routes: true` → gates routes via `ctx.can`.

## Client [#client]

`client.Todos.list()`, `client.Todos.create(data)`, `client.Todos.get(1)`, `client.Todos.update(1, data)`, `client.Todos.delete(1)` — see [Client SDK](/docs/api/client).


# API (/docs/api)



Kwiva's API layer turns one set of declarations into a complete, always-in-sync HTTP surface. From your `defineModel` and `defineController` files in `src/app/`, the framework derives a deterministic REST API, a fully typed RPC client, an OpenAPI 3.1 specification, Studio screens, and MCP tools — all through the same route manifest. The conventional REST surface, the generated model routes, and your own controller actions are not three separate systems. They are one system: deterministic model routes, custom controller actions, and a client that never drifts.

Everything in this section is derived. You never write route files twice, hand-maintain a spec, or regenerate a client SDK. The declarations are the contract, and every exported surface is a projection of the same route manifest.

## One Model, One Manifest [#one-model-one-manifest]

```plaintext title="one-model-one-manifest.txt"
src/app/models/posts.ts       defineModel('posts', ...)
src/app/http/controllers/     defineController('posts', ...)
                 │
                 ▼
           route manifest (IR)
                 │
   ┌──────┬──────┼─────┬──────┬──────┐
   ▼      ▼      ▼     ▼      ▼      ▼
 REST   RPC   OpenAPI  Studio  MCP  validation
```

The route manifest records path, method, schemas, response type, permission, and tags for every route — generated model routes and authored controller routes alike. `@kwiva/http` renders OpenAPI from it, `@kwiva/client` derives method types from it, and `@kwiva/mcp` exposes tools from it. Because every consumer reads the same intermediate representation, there is no second source of truth to keep in sync and no drift to fix.

## What the API Layer Includes [#what-the-api-layer-includes]

| Page                                                 | Covers                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [REST Conventions](/docs/api/rest)                   | URL patterns, method mapping, status codes, pagination, naming, error envelope |
| [Generated Endpoints](/docs/api/generated-endpoints) | The deterministic 5 routes per model, custom actions, permission gating        |
| [Typed RPC](/docs/api/rpc)                           | End-to-end types from controllers and models, zero runtime codegen             |
| [Client SDK](/docs/api/client)                       | `@kwiva/client`, SSR-safe usage, `createTestClient` for in-process tests       |
| [OpenAPI](/docs/api/openapi)                         | The auto-generated spec, `/openapi.json`, build artifact                       |
| [API Authentication](/docs/api/authentication)       | Session cookies, token sessions, middleware, per-route protection              |
| [API Errors](/docs/api/errors)                       | The error taxonomy, envelope shape, client-side typed handling                 |

The pages above read in two directions: conventions first for authors who shape the API, then the client and spec for consumers of it. Both directions meet in the manifest.

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

Define a model once — the framework generates the five standard routes:

```ts title="src/app/models/posts.ts"
// src/app/models/posts.ts
import { defineModel } from '@kwiva/data'

export default defineModel('posts', (f) => ({
  id: f.id(),
  title: f.string().validation((s) => s.min(1).max(200)),
  status: f.enum('draft', 'published').default('draft'),
}), { timestamps: true, permission: 'posts' })
```

Add custom behavior with a controller:

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/posts.ts"
// src/app/http/controllers/posts.ts
import { defineController } from '@kwiva/http'

export default defineController('posts', (c) => ({
  publish: c.post('/:id/publish', async ({ params }) => {
    const post = await Post.findOrFail(params.id)
    return post.update({ status: 'published', publishedAt: new Date() })
  }, { permission: 'posts.publish' }),
}), { prefix: '/posts', tags: ['posts'] })
```

Call the API with the typed client — every method, argument, and response type is inferred from the same definitions, with no codegen step:

```ts title="quick-start.ts"
import { createClient } from '@kwiva/client'

export const client = createClient({ baseUrl: 'https://api.acme.dev' })

const { data } = await client.posts.list({ page: 1 })
const post = await client.posts.get('pst_123')
await client.posts.publish('pst_123')
```

## The Endpoints [#the-endpoints]

* `/openapi.json` serves the generated OpenAPI 3.1 spec, with optional interactive docs at `/docs`.
* `/mcp` exposes model and controller routes as agent-callable tools when MCP is enabled.
* `/healthz` and `/readyz` provide liveness and readiness probes.

All rendered from the same manifest, all consistent with the routes you declared. See [OpenAPI](/docs/api/openapi) and the [MCP server](/docs/ai-mcp/mcp-server) pages.

## API and the HTTP Layer [#api-and-the-http-layer]

The API surface is the outward face of the HTTP layer. Controllers, middleware, guards, validation, and error mapping are declared in `@kwiva/http`; the API section documents the contract that surface produces — URLs, status codes, envelopes, and the typed client that consumes them. If you are writing routes, start with [Controllers](/docs/http/controllers); if you are designing the contract, start here.

## Generated vs Authored [#generated-vs-authored]

Two things produce routes. Knowing which handles a given path tells you where to change it:

| Path                           | Produced by        | Change by editing   |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------ | ------------------- |
| `/api/posts`, `/api/posts/:id` | `defineModel`      | the model file      |
| `/api/posts/:id/publish`       | `defineController` | the controller      |
| `/api/v1/...`                  | versioning config  | `src/config/api.ts` |
| `/openapi.json`, `/docs`       | manifest renderer  | nothing — automatic |
| `/healthz`, `/readyz`          | server routes      | `src/routes/*.ts`   |

The line is stable: model files own CRUD, controller files own custom behavior, server routes own infrastructure. Change one and the projections follow; there is no cross-editing between them.

## Conventions at a Glance [#conventions-at-a-glance]

* Collections are lowercase plural; custom segments are kebab-case; no verbs in paths.
* Five deterministic routes per model, plus custom actions.
* `PATCH` is partial, `DELETE` returns 204, lists use the paginated envelope.
* All failures share one taxonomy and one envelope.
* The typed client is the reference consumer; OpenAPI is the reference document.

These are not preferences; they are the contract tooling depends on.

## The API Lifecycle, End to End [#the-api-lifecycle-end-to-end]

A call to `client.posts.list({ page: 1 })` travels the same pipeline as a raw `curl`: parse, validation, guards, handler, serialization. On the server the client skips the network hop but not the pipeline — policies and validation still run, which keeps in-process calls honest. See [Request Lifecycle](/docs/http/lifecycle) and [Generated Endpoints](/docs/api/generated-endpoints).

## REST, Generated, and Custom Actions [#rest-generated-and-custom-actions]

Routes fall into three authored shapes that stay consistent:

* Model-generated CRUD — five routes per model, permissions from the model option
* Custom actions — one route per action, declared in the controller
* REST-only — plain paths, full control

The three share validation, guards, the envelope, the client, and the spec. See [Generated Endpoints](/docs/api/generated-endpoints) and [REST Conventions](/docs/api/rest).

## Auth and Permissions in One Sentence [#auth-and-permissions-in-one-sentence]

Authentication answers who is calling; authorization answers what they may do. The `auth` middleware asserts a session, guards assert specifics, and route `permission` keys assert ability. See [API Authentication](/docs/api/authentication) and [Authorization](/docs/authorization).

## The Versioned Contract [#the-versioned-contract]

The API ships under a versioning policy you configure once. Public behavior that callers depend on — method names, request shapes, response envelopes, error codes — changes only across a version bump, never silently within one. See [REST conventions: versioning](/docs/api/rest).

## What the Framework Enforces [#what-the-framework-enforces]

The manifest is the single source of truth for routes, schemas, permissions, and tags. Because every projection — client, OpenAPI, MCP, Studio, the dev overlay — derives from it, the framework enforces consistency at the architecture level: a route that contradicts the manifest, a client method that drifts from a route, or a policy that lacks a route cannot exist quietly. The section pages that follow are the detailed statements of that contract.

## What's Next [#whats-next]

* [REST Conventions](/docs/api/rest) — the URL, status code, and envelope contract
* [Typed RPC](/docs/api/rpc) — how types flow end-to-end without codegen
* [Controllers](/docs/http/controllers) — the `defineController` surface
* [Models](/docs/data/models) — the `defineModel` source of truth
* [Your First API](/docs/getting-started/first-api) — build an API from scratch


# OpenAPI (/docs/api/openapi)



# OpenAPI [#openapi]

Auto-generated from the route manifest. Mount via `mountOpenAPI(app, manifest)`.

## Output [#output]

* `/openapi.json` — OpenAPI 3.1 spec
* `/docs` — Scalar docs UI

## Options [#options]

`OpenAPIOptions{title?, version?, description?, path?, specPath?, scalar?, documentation?, exclude?, models?}`.

## Model schema shaping [#model-schema-shaping]

`fieldToJsonSchema`, `modelToJsonSchema`, `modelSchemas`, `manifestReferences` — from `@kwiva/http`.

> \[!TIP]
> Add models to the manifest via `bootApp(server, {models})` → auto-appears in spec.


# REST Conventions (/docs/api/rest)



# REST Conventions [#rest-conventions]

Kwiva auto-generates REST per model (5 routes). These are the conventions.

## URL Structure [#url-structure]

```
/api/{model}         # list/create
/api/{model}/:id     # get/update/remove
```

## Methods & status [#methods--status]

| Route                        | Method    | Status       |
| ---------------------------- | --------- | ------------ |
| `GET /api/{model}`           | GET       | 200 (list)   |
| `POST /api/{model}`          | POST      | 201 (create) |
| `GET /api/{model}/:id`       | GET       | 200          |
| `PATCH/PUT /api/{model}/:id` | PATCH/PUT | 200          |
| `DELETE /api/{model}/:id`    | DELETE    | 200/204      |

## Envelope [#envelope]

```json
{
  "data": { ... },
  "pagination": { "page": 1, "size": 20, "total": 42 }
}
```

List responses: `data` is array (or `{items, cursor?}` for cursor pagination).

## Errors [#errors]

See [Errors](/docs/api/errors) — 8-code taxonomy.

## Auth [#auth]

`GET /session` for session check (via `ctx.session`); `requireAuth` on protected routes; permissions via `{resource}.{action}`.

## Model → route name [#model--route-name]

`registerModel('posts')` → `/api/posts`; `toSnakeCase(pluralize('post')) = "posts"`.


# Typed RPC (/docs/api/rpc)



# Typed RPC [#typed-rpc]

Zero-codegen typed client from `src/.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts`.

## `client` singleton [#client-singleton]

```ts
import { client } from "@kwiva/client";
const todos = await client.Todos.list({ query: { page: 1 } });
const todo = await client.Todos.get({ params: { id: 42 } });
```

## `initClient` / `resetClient` / `getClientSnapshot` [#initclient--resetclient--getclientsnapshot]

```ts
import { initClient, resetClient } from "@kwiva/client";
initClient({ baseUrl: "https://api.example.com", credentials: "include" });
```

## `callRoute` [#callroute]

```ts
import { callRoute } from "@kwiva/client";
await callRoute("TodosController.list");
```

## Typed `RouteTree` [#typed-routetree]

`ClientRegister{routes}` — from `src/.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts`; `TypedClient<R>` wraps Eden Treaty with typed method access.

## SSR/Test [#ssrtest]

`getClientSnapshot()` for SSR; `@kwiva/testing` `withApp()` returns `ctx.client`.

> \[!TIP]
> Handlers register by route id — `findRoute(entries, name)` at runtime.


# Client-Side Auth (/docs/auth/client-usage)



# Client-Side Auth [#client-side-auth]

`@kwiva/auth` client hooks — React peer deps (`react`, `react-dom`).

## `useSession(endpoint = "/session")` [#usesessionendpoint--session]

```tsx
const { session, user, isLoading, refresh } = useSession();
```

## `useCan(ability)` / `AbilitiesProvider` [#usecanability--abilitiesprovider]

## SSR [#ssr]

`ssrSafeAuth()` — session read without redirects during SSR.

## Login flow [#login-flow]

1. Submit credentials → `POST /auth/login`
2. Kwiva sets `kwiva_session` cookie → reload or soft-navigate

## Logout [#logout]

`POST /auth/logout` → clear cookies.

> \[!TIP]
> Built-in hooks: `useSession`, `AbilitiesProvider`, `useCan`, `setAmbientAbilities`, `getAmbientAbilities`.


# Auth Configuration (/docs/auth/configuration)



# Auth Configuration [#auth-configuration]

File: `src/config/auth.ts`.

```ts
export default defineAuth({
  providers: [emailPassword(), magicLink(), oauth({ id: "google", clientId, clientSecret })],
  session: {
    secret: "dev-only-secret", // non-empty
    maxAge: 604800, // seconds, positive
    cookie: { name: "kwiva_session", httpOnly: true, secure: false, sameSite: "lax" },
  },
  register: { createUser: async ({ email, password }) => ({ email, password }), minPasswordLength: 8 },
  remember: { maxAge: 31536000 },
  rateLimit: { login: { max: 5, windowMs: 60000 } },
  trustProxy: true,
});
```

## `AuthConfig` [#authconfig]

| Key          | Type                   | Notes                                                                                                                            |
| ------------ | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `providers`  | `AuthProviderConfig[]` | from `emailPassword()`, `magicLink()`, `oauth(provider)`                                                                         |
| `session`    | `AuthSessionConfig`    | `{secret, maxAge, cookie?}` — `AuthCookieOptions{name?, httpOnly?, secure?, sameSite?: "lax"\|"strict"\|"none", path?, domain?}` |
| `register`   | `RegisterConfig`       | `{createUser(input): User, minPasswordLength? (≥1)}`; input `{email, password}`                                                  |
| `remember`   | `RememberConfig`       | `{maxAge?, cookie?}`                                                                                                             |
| `rateLimit`  | `RateLimitConfig`      | `{login?: {max, windowMs}}`                                                                                                      |
| `trustProxy` | `boolean \| int ≥ 0`   | —                                                                                                                                |

## Cookie defaults [#cookie-defaults]

* Session cookie: `kwiva_session`, httpOnly, secure:false, sameSite: lax, path `/`.
* Remember cookie: `kwiva_remember` (365d default).

## `validateAuthConfig` [#validateauthconfig]

Throws `TypeError` on malformed shapes (via `applyConfigSections` in boot seam).

## Key locations [#key-locations]

| Symbol               | Package     | Where                       |
| -------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------- |
| `defineAuth`         | @kwiva/auth | `packages/auth/src/config/` |
| `validateAuthConfig` | @kwiva/auth | same                        |

> \[!TIP]
> For zero-argument defaults, omit `providers` — Kwiva will fail validation if session has no users.

# Protecting Routes (/docs/auth/protecting-routes)



# Protecting Routes [#protecting-routes]

## `requireAuth()` — wraps handlers; puts `ctx.session`/`ctx.user` on context. [#requireauth--wraps-handlers-puts-ctxsessionctxuser-on-context]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/private.ts"
export const PrivateController = defineController({
  prefix: "/api/private",
  middleware: [requireAuth()],
  routes(api) {
    api.get("/", async (ctx) => ({ user: ctx.user?.email }));
  },
});
```

## `guestOnly({redirectTo})` — redirects authed users. [#guestonlyredirectto--redirects-authed-users]

## Verify flows [#verify-flows]

* 403 `FORBIDDEN` for unverified emails (`verified()` middleware).
* 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` on missing session.

## Client [#client]

`useSession()` — returns `{session, user, isLoading, refresh}`.

> \[!TIP]
> 401 vs 403: Kwiva uses 401 for missing sessions (UNAUTHORIZED), 403 for verified-required/missing session.


# Auth Providers (/docs/auth/providers)



# Auth Providers [#auth-providers]

## Built-in providers [#built-in-providers]

| Provider       | Factory                   | Flow                                         |
| -------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Email/password | `emailPassword()`         | register, login, reset via email             |
| Magic link     | `magicLink()`             | `POST /auth/login` sends link                |
| OAuth          | `oauth(provider, hooks?)` | PKCE, redirect to provider, `/auth/callback` |

Provider descriptors: `{kind, resolveUser?, verify?}` — customize user resolution per provider.

## Routes [#routes]

Providers create controllers on the fly; see [Client-Side Auth](/docs/auth/client-usage).

## Status codes [#status-codes]

* 401 `UNAUTHORIZED` for missing/invalid session
* 403 `FORBIDDEN` for failed login (don't leak if email invalid? — Kwiva says 403)

## Identity flows [#identity-flows]

* Password reset: `createPasswordReset` → verify + reset
* Email verification: `createEmailVerifier`, `isEmailVerified`
* Magic links: `createMagicLink`
* TOTP + recovery codes: `generateTotpSecret`, `totpCode`, `generateRecoveryCodes`
* PKCE OAuth: `createPkcePair`, `createOAuthClient`

## When to use [#when-to-use]

* Social login for B2B/ecommerce
* Password for forms (Kwiva primary)


# Sessions (/docs/auth/sessions)



# Sessions [#sessions]

## Cookie-based sessions [#cookie-based-sessions]

```ts
import { createSession, getSession, commitSession, destroySessionCookie } from "@kwiva/auth";

const session = await createSession(user);
// → session.id (HMAC-signed cookie value), cookie via commitSession(session)
```

## API [#api]

| API                                   | Notes                                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `createSession(user, options?)`       | → `Session{id, userId, expiresAt}`    |
| `getSession(request, options?)`       | → `Session \| null`                   |
| `rotateSession(sessionId, options?)`  | rotate                                |
| `refreshSession(sessionId, options?)` | extend                                |
| `destroySession(sessionId, options?)` | invalidate                            |
| `commitSession(session, options?)`    | `Set-Cookie` string                   |
| `destroySessionCookie(cookie?)`       | expiry cookie                         |
| `resolveSessionParams(ctx, options?)` | → `{secret, maxAge?, cookie?, store}` |

## Implementation details [#implementation-details]

* HMAC-SHA256 cookie signing (`serializeSessionValue`/`parseSessionValue`).
* scrypt password hashing (`hashPassword`/`verifyPassword`).

## Client: `useSession(endpoint="/session")` [#client-usesessionendpointsession]

Returns `{session, user, isLoading, refresh}` — from GET `/session`.


# Enforcement Points (/docs/authorization/enforcement)



# Enforcement Points [#enforcement-points]

Authorization is enforced at multiple layers:

| Surface          | Enforcement                              |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Generated routes | `model.options.permission` via `ctx.can` |
| Controllers      | `ctx.can` / `authorize(policy, ...)`     |
| WS channels      | `channel().policy(fn)`                   |
| MCP tools        | `ability` + `ctx.can`                    |
| Seeders/tasks    | `ctx.can` ambient checks (where used)    |

> \[!TIP]
> Check at every boundary — defense in depth, not a single gate.


# Authorization (/docs/authorization)



# Authorization [#authorization]

Three layers:

1. **Policies** (`definePolicy`) — per-resource logic (`can(post, user, "delete")`)
2. **Gates** (`defineGate`) — standalone allow/deny hooks
3. **Permissions** (`resource.action` strings) — used by generated routes (`ctx.can`)

## Entry points [#entry-points]

| Topic                               | Page                                           |
| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Policies                            | [Policies](/docs/authorization/policies)       |
| Permissions (`{resource}.{action}`) | [Permissions](/docs/authorization/permissions) |
| Roles                               | [RBAC](/docs/authorization/roles)              |
| Enforcement points                  | [Enforcement](/docs/authorization/enforcement) |


# Permissions (/docs/authorization/permissions)



# Permissions [#permissions]

## Grammar [#grammar]

`{resource}.{action}` — e.g. `posts.read`, `todos.create`. Defined at policies: `definePolicy({...})` or `PolicyRule`.

## Gating [#gating]

* Generated routes: `model.options.permission` → gates via `ctx.can(permission)` at runtime (against `ctx.user`).
* `ctx.can` — ambient ALS scope; `can(permission, resource?)` boolean; `authorize`/`authorizeGate` throw.

## API [#api]

| API                                          | Notes                                            |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `ctx.can(permission, resource?)`             | boolean                                          |
| `ctx.canOrThrow()` / `authorize(permission)` | throws ForbiddenError                            |
| `PolicyRegistry{register, resolve}`          | `getDefaultRegistry/policyFor/normalizeRegistry` |

> \[!TIP]
> See [Policies](/docs/authorization/policies) for the definition.


# Policies (/docs/authorization/policies)



# Policies [#policies]

## `definePolicy(rules, options?)` [#definepolicyrules-options]

```ts title="src/app/policies/post.ts"
import { definePolicy } from "@kwiva/auth";

export const PostPolicy = definePolicy({
  delete(user, post) { return post.authorId === user.id; },
  edit(user, post) { return post.authorId === user.id && !post.published; },
}, {
  before(user, resource) { return user?.admin === true; },
});
```

Policies are frozen at runtime. Default deny.

## `defineGate(check)` [#definegatecheck]

```ts title="src/app/policies/admin.ts"
import { defineGate } from "@kwiva/auth";
export const AdminGate = defineGate((user) => user?.role === "admin");
```

## APIs [#apis]

| API                                          | Notes                                |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `can(policy, user, action, resource?)`       | explicit; throws ForbiddenError      |
| `cannot`                                     | —                                    |
| `authorize(policy, user, action, resource?)` | throws on deny                       |
| `authorizeGate(gate, user, resource?)`       | —                                    |
| `whereCan(...)`                              | boolean variant (ambient + explicit) |

## Ambient (ALS) usage [#ambient-als-usage]

```ts
import { can } from "@kwiva/auth";
can("edit"); // uses currentAuth() scope
```

> \[!TIP]
> Register via `src/app/policies/` — discovered automatically by the policies folder convention.


# RBAC (/docs/authorization/roles)



# RBAC [#rbac]

Roles are just data — add `role` to `@kwiva/auth` user store:

```ts title="src/app/models/user.ts"
export const User = defineModel("users", (f) => ({
  id: f.id(),
  email: f.string().validation((v) => v.min(3).max(255)),
  name: f.string().optional(),
  role: f.string().default("member"),
}), { timestamps: true });
```

## Policy interpretation [#policy-interpretation]

`definePolicy` rules check roles:

```ts
export const AdminPolicy = definePolicy({
  read(user) { return user?.role === "admin"; },
});
```

## Enforcement [#enforcement]

Enforced at: generated routes (permissions), custom controllers (`ctx.can`), channels, MCP tools, tasks.

> \[!TIP]
> Roles are optional — `defineAuth` validates `role` if present in `User`.


# Background Work (/docs/background-work)



# Background Work [#background-work]

| Topic             | Page                                                     |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Jobs (defineJob)  | [Jobs](/docs/background-work/jobs)                       |
| Queues & Workers  | [Queues & Workers](/docs/background-work/queues)         |
| Scheduled Tasks   | [Scheduled Tasks](/docs/background-work/scheduling)      |
| Job Observability | [Job Observability](/docs/background-work/observability) |

## Model of work [#model-of-work]

```
defineJob ──► dispatch() ──► queue ──► worker ──► retry loop
```

## Related [#related]

* [@kwiva/jobs API](/api/jobs) — full public surface (dispatch, outbox, middleware, cron, metrics)


# Jobs (/docs/background-work/jobs)



# Jobs [#jobs]

## defineJob [#definejob]

```ts title="src/app/jobs/send-welcome.ts"
import { defineJob } from "@kwiva/jobs";

export const SendWelcomeJob = defineJob({
  handler(input) {
    // do work
  },
  onSuccess() { /* audit */ },
  onFailure() { /* retry/audit */ },
});
```

## Job options (full) [#job-options-full]

| Field         | Notes                                               |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `queue`       | target queue (default `default`)                    |
| `tries`       | max attempts (default 5)                            |
| `backoff`     | `{strategy: "fixed"\|"exponential", baseMs, maxMs}` |
| `timeoutMs`   | —                                                   |
| `jitter`      | default true                                        |
| `unique`      | `{key(input), ttlMs?}`                              |
| `afterCommit` | run after response                                  |
| `priority`    | queue priority                                      |
| `encrypted`   | AES-256-GCM payload                                 |
| `middleware`  | `[throttle, withoutOverlap, ...]`                   |
| `input`       | Standard Schema for input validation                |

## Dispatch [#dispatch]

`dispatch(job, input, {queue?, delayMs?, runAt?, priority?, afterCommit?})` → `Promise<string>` (record id).

`dispatchSync(job, input)` — one attempt, throws on failure.

## Retry logic [#retry-logic]

On failure: decrement tries, requeue with backoff; `JobReleaseError{delayMs}` — for manual retry.

## Idempotency [#idempotency]

`unique: {key(input), ttlMs}` — dedupes; `claimUnique/releaseUnique/settleUnique`.

## Dead letters [#dead-letters]

On exhausted retries: `failedJobs()`, `retryFailed(id)`.

> \[!TIP]
> `dispatchAfterResponse` — for "send after response" flows.


# Job Observability (/docs/background-work/observability)



# Job Observability [#job-observability]

## Metrics [#metrics]

```ts
import { queueMetrics } from "@kwiva/jobs";
queueMetrics(); // {pending, pendingByQueue, failed, processed, succeeded, inFlight, workers}
```

## Events [#events]

`onJobEvent(event, handler)` — events: `processing | retrying | processed | failed`.

## Failed jobs [#failed-jobs]

`failedJobs()` — `FailedJob{id, queue, attempts, input, error, errorCode?, failedAt}`.

## Retry [#retry]

`retryFailed(id)`, `retryAllFailed()`.

## Logs [#logs]

`ctx.logger` in worker — structured JSON via `@kwiva/core` logger.

## Dev overlay [#dev-overlay]

Available in dev — see [Dev Overlay](/docs/observability/dev-overlay).


# Queues & Workers (/docs/background-work/queues)



# Queues & Workers [#queues--workers]

## In-memory queue (default) [#in-memory-queue-default]

```ts
import { createMemoryQueue, setDefaultEngine } from "@kwiva/jobs";
setDefaultEngine(createMemoryQueue());
```

## Workers [#workers]

```ts
import { startWorker } from "@kwiva/jobs";
const worker = startWorker({ queues: ["default"], concurrency: 4 });
// later: await worker.stop()
```

## Concurrency [#concurrency]

`concurrency` (default 4) — parallel job executions.

## Polling [#polling]

Workers poll `due(now, queue?)`; default poll 100ms, `maxPollMs` 5s.

## Custom engines [#custom-engines]

`setDefaultEngine/getDefaultEngine/resetDefaultEngine`.

## Outbox [#outbox]

`enqueueOutbox/drainOutbox` — after-commit.

> \[!TIP]
> pg-boss is an opt-in transport (`@kwiva/jobs-pg-boss`).


# Scheduled Tasks (/docs/background-work/scheduling)



# Scheduled Tasks [#scheduled-tasks]

## defineTask [#definetask]

```ts title="src/app/tasks/cleanup.ts"
import { defineTask } from "@kwiva/jobs";

export const CleanupOldLogs = defineTask({
  schedule: "0 2 * * *", // cron 5-field
  description: "Cleanup old logs",
  preventOverlapping: true,
  handler: async ({ logger, now }) => { /* cleanup */ },
});
```

## Cron [#cron]

`parseCron(expr)` — 5-field + macros (`@yearly` … `@minutely`).

## Scheduler [#scheduler]

`startScheduler({tasks, tickMs, timezone})` → `{tick, stop}`.

## Timezone [#timezone]

IANA timezones supported.

## Management [#management]

`withoutOverlapping(task)`, `assertValidTimeZone`, `runTask(task)` — manual run.

> \[!TIP]
> Start scheduler in `bootstrap/app.ts` or via `kwiva start`? No — `kwiva dev` includes scheduler if configured.


# Addon Commands (/docs/cli/addon-commands)



# Addon Commands [#addon-commands]

> **Not implemented.** The Kwiva framework repo has no addons system at this time. This page is kept as a stub for future adoption. See [modules-plugins](/docs/modules-plugins) for what IS implemented (defineModule/definePlugin).


# Database Commands (/docs/cli/database-commands)



# Database Commands [#database-commands]

| Command                  | Purpose                                         |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `kwiva migrate`          | Apply migrations from `src/database/migrations` |
| `kwiva migrate:status`   | Print `applied: ...` / `pending: ...`           |
| `kwiva migrate:down`     | Roll back last batch                            |
| `kwiva migrate:generate` | Generate DDL diffs from model IR                |
| `kwiva seed`             | Run all seeders (`src/database/seeders`)        |
| `kwiva seed <name>`      | Run one seeder by name                          |

## Storage [#storage]

| Command                                | Purpose                                             |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `kwiva storage:sync <from> <to>`       | Copy objects between disks; `[--prune] [--dry-run]` |
| `kwiva storage:clear [disk] [--force]` | Clear a disk (S3/GCS/Azure/Blob need force)         |

## Search [#search]

`kwiva search:reindex [model]` — requires `database` section.

## MCP [#mcp]

`kwiva mcp` / `kwiva mcp:print-config` — see [AI & MCP](/docs/ai-mcp).

> \[!TIP]
> `kwiva doctor` checks all DB/search/MCP health first.


# Generators (/docs/cli/generators)



# Generators [#generators]

`kwiva make:<kind> <Name>` — one per construct. Each writes to its conventional folder.

## Full list [#full-list]

| Kind         | Target                     | Suffix              |
| ------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------- |
| `config`     | `src/config`               | —                   |
| `service`    | `src/app/services`         | `Service`           |
| `model`      | `src/app/models`           | —                   |
| `controller` | `src/app/http/controllers` | `Controller`        |
| `middleware` | `src/app/http/middleware`  | `Middleware`        |
| `contract`   | `src/app/http/contracts`   | `Contract`          |
| `policy`     | `src/app/policies`         | `Policy`            |
| `gate`       | `src/app/policies`         | `Gate`              |
| `job`        | `src/app/jobs`             | `Job`               |
| `task`       | `src/app/tasks`            | `Task`              |
| `event`      | `src/app/events`           | `Event`             |
| `listener`   | `src/app/events`           | `Listener`          |
| `mail`       | `src/app/mail`             | `Mail`              |
| `factory`    | `src/database/factories`   | `Factory`           |
| `migration`  | `src/database/migrations`  | `Migration` (dated) |
| `seeder`     | `src/database/seeders`     | `Seeder`            |
| `page`       | `src/ui/pages`             | `Page`              |
| `mcp-tool`   | `src/app/mcp/tools`        | `Tool`              |
| `command`    | `src/app/commands`         | `Command`           |

Examples:

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva make:model Todo
kwiva make:controller Todos
kwiva make:policy Posts
kwiva make:job SendWelcome
kwiva make:migration 20260101000000_create_posts
```

## Output shape [#output-shape]

Generator writes minimal valid `defineX` file — e.g.:

```ts title="src/app/jobs/send-welcome.ts"
import { defineJob } from "@kwiva/jobs";
export const SendWelcomeJob = defineJob({
  handler: async (input) => { /* work */ },
});
```

> \[!TIP]
> Run generators before diving into the app — they're the canonical starting points.

# CLI [#cli]

## Framework commands [#framework-commands]

| Command                                                      | Description                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `kwiva create <name>`                                        | Scaffold new app            |

| `kwiva test`                                                 | `bun test` wrapper          |

| `kwiva seed [name]`                                          | Seed (all/one seeder)       |
| `kwiva task <name>`                                          | Run a task                  |
| `kwiva route:list`                                           | List routes                 |
| `kwiva key:generate`                                         | Generate APP\_KEY           |
| `kwiva storage:sync <from> <to>`                             | Storage migration           |
| `kwiva storage:clear [disk]`                                 | Clear disk                  |
| `kwiva search:reindex [model]`                               | Reindex FTS                 |
| `kwiva mcp` / `kwiva mcp:print-config`                       | MCP server + config         |
| `kwiva doctor`                                               | Health checks               |

# Project Commands (/docs/cli/project-commands)



# Project Commands [#project-commands]

## `kwiva create <name>` [#kwiva-create-name]

`kwiva create my-app` — scaffolds `bootstrap/`, `src/config/{app,database,cache,kv,storage,mcp}.ts`, `src/app/models/`, `src/app/http/controllers/`, `src/database/{migrations,seeders}/`, `package.json` scripts. Logs `kwiva create → scaffolded <target>`.

## `kwiva dev [--port <n>]` [#kwiva-dev---port-n]

Development server. Default port 3000. Hot-reload of client changes.

## `kwiva build [--out <dir>]` [#kwiva-build---out-dir]

Bundles + route-tree codegen. Default out: `dist`.

## `kwiva test` [#kwiva-test]

`bun test` wrapper.

# Architecture (/docs/contributing/architecture)



# Architecture for Contributors [#architecture-for-contributors]

See [Package Boundaries](/docs/advanced/package-boundaries) for the full map.

## Core rules [#core-rules]

* App code imports only `@kwiva/*`
* Engines sealed (oxlint `no-engine-imports` gate)
* Package graph acyclic

## Adding a new factory [#adding-a-new-factory]

1. Add factory to `@kwiva/<pkg>`
2. Register in discover.ts if app-facing
3. Update definex.mdx (documented)
4. Add API page (api/\*.mdx)
5. Test it

## Coding standards [#coding-standards]

* strict TS, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`
* oxlint + tsc + eslint parity

## Tests [#tests]

Run: `bun test` in package dir; add colocated tests (`*.test.ts`).


# Development Environment (/docs/contributing/development-environment)



# Development Environment [#development-environment]

## Prereqs [#prereqs]

* **Bun** ≥ 1.4.0 (`engines`)
* Git
* Editor with TS support (VSCode/Cursor; oxlint for lint)

## Setup [#setup]

```bash title="terminal"
git clone https://github.com/kwiva/kwiva
cd kwiva
bun install
bun test
bun run typecheck
```

## Tools [#tools]

* **oxlint** — lint (`oxlint src`)
* **tsc** — types via `bun run typecheck`
* **bunx tsc --noEmit\`**
* **croner** (jobs), etc.

## IDE [#ide]

VSCode + TypeScript, TS 5.7/5.9; strict mode on.

## Getting started [#getting-started]

Try building an example:

```bash
bun run examples/todo-app-m3
cd examples/todo-app-m3
bun run dev
```

# PR Guidelines (/docs/contributing/pr-guidelines)



# PR Guidelines [#pr-guidelines]

* PR title: `type(scope): description` (`feat(auth): add OAuth PKCE`)
* Body: what changed, why, how tested, related ADR (if any)
* CI must pass (typecheck + test + build + functionality gates)

See [Releases](/docs/contributing/releases).


# Releases (/docs/contributing/releases)



# Releases [#releases]

## Changesets [#changesets]

Kwiva uses changesets (`.changeset/`):

* Add a changeset file in `.changeset/` for user-facing changes
* `bunx changeset status` to see pending

## Versioning [#versioning]

Packages: `@kwiva/*` — see [Versioning](/reference/versioning).

## Branch rules [#branch-rules]

* `main` — only from approved PRs (squash-merge)
* `feat/`, `fix/`, `chore/` — short-lived

## Checklist [#checklist]

* [ ] Changeset added
* [ ] Tests pass (`bun test`)
* [ ] Lint passes (`oxlint`)
* [ ] Typecheck passes (`bun run typecheck`)
* [ ] API docs updated (if public)


# Testing Standards (/docs/contributing/testing)



# Testing Standards [#testing-standards]

## Tests live [#tests-live]

`packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts` (colocated).

## Stack [#stack]

* `bun:test`
* `@kwiva/testing` harness
* `@electric-sql/pglite` (dev)

## Quality gates [#quality-gates]

* `bun test` per package (in-repo)
* `bun run ci` (typecheck + test + build + functionality)

See also [@kwiva/testing docs](/api/testing).


# Applications (/docs/core-concepts/applications)



# Applications [#applications]

```ts title="bootstrap/app.ts"
import { defineApp } from "@kwiva/core";

export default defineApp({
  name: "my-app",
  // additive:
  models: [], controllers: [], policies: [], pages: [],
  jobs: [], events: [], tasks: [], commands: [],
});
```

## API [#api]

| API                       | Notes                                          |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `defineApp(options)`      | returns `AppDefinition`; no classes/decorators |
| `assembleApp(app, root?)` | → `UnitRegistry` — discovery + merge           |

## Composition [#composition]

`defineApp` is additive — multiple arrays merge without duplicates (throws on name conflicts).

## Boot [#boot]

1. `kwiva create` — writes `bootstrap/app.ts`
2. `kwiva dev`/`bun src/index.ts` — imports `bootstrap/app.ts`
3. `assembleApp` — registers everything

## Modules [#modules]

`modules: [TodosModule]` — see [Modules](/docs/modules-plugins/defining-modules).


# Auto-Discovery (/docs/core-concepts/auto-discovery)



# Auto-Discovery [#auto-discovery]

`discoverKind(root, kind)` scans conventional folders and registers units by exported const name.

## Discovery map [#discovery-map]

| Kind          | Folder                     | Mode      |
| ------------- | -------------------------- | --------- |
| `models`      | `src/app/models`           | flat      |
| `services`    | `src/app/services`         | flat      |
| `policies`    | `src/app/policies`         | flat      |
| `jobs`        | `src/app/jobs`             | flat      |
| `events`      | `src/app/events`           | flat      |
| `tasks`       | `src/app/tasks`            | flat      |
| `commands`    | `src/app/commands`         | flat      |
| `controllers` | `src/app/http/controllers` | flat      |
| `middleware`  | `src/app/http/middleware`  | flat      |
| `pages`       | `src/ui/pages`             | recursive |

See [feature inventory](/docs/research/feature-inventory) for the full map + CLI extras.


# Configuration (/docs/core-concepts/configuration)



# Configuration [#configuration]

See [Getting Started → Configuration](/docs/getting-started/configuration) — same content, canonical location.

Key points:

* Files in `src/config/*.ts`, section = filename
* Precedence: built-ins → files → env
* `defineConfig` — pass-through validator


# Context (/docs/core-concepts/context)



# Context [#context]

## `ctx` (`HttpContext`) [#ctx-httpcontext]

```ts
ctx.input        // {params, query, body, headers, cookies}
ctx.headers()    // headers
ctx.setHeaders() // set response headers
ctx.json()/ctx.text()/ctx.noContent()/ctx.redirect()/ctx.stream()
ctx.session      // via requireAuth
ctx.user         // via requireAuth
ctx.can          // ambient ability check
ctx.waitUntil(p) // after-response
ctx.store        // app store access
```

## ALS scopes (context + ALS) [#als-scopes-context--als]

* `runWithRequest` / `currentRequest`
* `runWithAuth` / `currentAuth` — `{user, policies?}`
* `runWithTenant` / `currentTenant`
* `runInTransaction` / `onTransactionCommit/Rollback`

## Session lifecycle [#session-lifecycle]

* Session created via `requireAuth` → cookie via `commitSession`.
* `ctx.user` attach — policy checks via `ctx.can`.


# The defineX Convention (/docs/core-concepts/definex)



# The defineX Convention [#the-definex-convention]

## What is defineX? [#what-is-definex]

`defineX` is Kwiva's unifying abstraction: every app-facing construct is a factory function producing a frozen, serializable definition (the "one definition"). Reading Kwiva app code should feel like reading a description of the product.

## The Complete Surface (app-facing factories, 19 total) [#the-complete-surface-app-facing-factories-19-total]

| Factory            | Purpose                          | Package         |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------- | --------------- |
| `defineApp`        | Application composition          | `@kwiva/core`   |
| `defineConfig`     | Config sections                  | `@kwiva/core`   |
| `defineService`    | Services                         | `@kwiva/core`   |
| `defineModel`      | Data models                      | `@kwiva/data`   |
| `defineController` | HTTP controllers                 | `@kwiva/http`   |
| `defineContract`   | Typed request/response contracts | `@kwiva/http`   |
| `defineMiddleware` | Middleware                       | `@kwiva/http`   |
| `definePage`       | Frontend pages                   | `@kwiva/ui`     |
| `defineIsland`     | Client islands                   | `@kwiva/ui`     |
| `defineJob`        | Background jobs                  | `@kwiva/jobs`   |
| `defineTask`       | Scheduled tasks                  | `@kwiva/jobs`   |
| `defineEvent`      | Events                           | `@kwiva/events` |
| `defineListener`   | Event listeners                  | `@kwiva/events` |
| `defineSubscriber` | Subscribers                      | `@kwiva/events` |
| `defineMail`       | Mail                             | `@kwiva/mail`   |
| `defineMcpTool`    | MCP tools                        | `@kwiva/mcp`    |
| `definePolicy`     | Authorization policies           | `@kwiva/auth`   |
| `defineGate`       | Authorization gates              | `@kwiva/auth`   |
| `defineCommand`    | CLI app commands                 | `@kwiva/cli`    |

### Companion DSLs (extending the grammar) [#companion-dsls-extending-the-grammar]

| DSL                                      | Where            | Purpose                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------- | -------------------------- |
| `defineSeeder`                           | data             | idempotent seeding         |
| `defineFactory`                          | data             | test factories for models  |
| `defineMigration`                        | data             | timestamped SQL migrations |
| `defineRedisStore` / `installRedisStore` | store            | opt-in Redis StoreDriver   |
| `defineSmtpTransport`                    | mail-smtp        | Nodemailer SMTP transport  |
| `defineResendTransport`                  | mail-resend      | Resend API transport       |
| `definePgBossQueue`                      | jobs-pg-boss     | opt-in pg-boss transport   |
| `defineBetterAuth` + `mountBetterAuth`   | auth-better-auth | sealed Better Auth engine  |

### Packages map (app-facing) [#packages-map-app-facing]

| Package         | Factories it owns                                                 |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@kwiva/core`   | `defineApp`, `defineConfig`, `defineService`                      |
| `@kwiva/data`   | `defineModel`, `defineSeeder`, `defineFactory`, `defineMigration` |
| `@kwiva/http`   | `defineController`, `defineContract`, `defineMiddleware`          |
| `@kwiva/ui`     | `definePage`, `defineIsland`                                      |
| `@kwiva/client` | — (hooks)                                                         |
| `@kwiva/jobs`   | `defineJob`, `defineTask`                                         |
| `@kwiva/events` | `defineEvent`, `defineListener`, `defineSubscriber`               |
| `@kwiva/mail`   | `defineMail`                                                      |
| `@kwiva/mcp`    | `defineMcpTool`                                                   |
| `@kwiva/auth`   | `definePolicy`, `defineGate`                                      |
| `@kwiva/cli`    | `defineCommand`                                                   |

## Convention rules [#convention-rules]

### One construct per file [#one-construct-per-file]

Each factory produces one unit; files export it as a named const ending in the suffix: `TodosController`, `HelloPage`, `SendReminderJob`, `CreatePostContract`, etc.

### Where files live [#where-files-live]

Auto-discovered by convention. Full map (from `discover.ts DEFAULT_FOLDERS`):

| Construct           | Folder                      | Notes                                      |
| ------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Model               | `src/app/models/`           | flat                                       |
| Controller          | `src/app/http/controllers/` | flat                                       |
| Middleware          | `src/app/http/middleware/`  | flat                                       |
| Policy/Gate         | `src/app/policies/`         | flat                                       |
| Service             | `src/app/services/`         | flat                                       |
| Job                 | `src/app/jobs/`             | flat                                       |
| Task                | `src/app/tasks/`            | flat                                       |
| Event               | `src/app/events/`           | flat                                       |
| Listener/Subscriber | `src/app/events/`           | flat                                       |
| Page                | `src/ui/pages/`             | **recursive** (`$param`, `$`, nested dirs) |

`src/app/mcp/tools/` — MCP tools; `src/app/commands/` — app commands (CLI). `src/app/mail/` — **not** in DEFAULT\_FOLDERS; config-driven via `setMailConfig` in the boot seam.

### Inline options [#inline-options]

Every factory takes options as a **second argument or `(f) => ({...})` map** with full type inference and runtime validation. No decorators, no classes, no global registries.

### Freeze + dedupe [#freeze--dedupe]

All definitions are frozen at runtime; duplicate names throw (`defineModel`, `bindRouteIds`, etc.).

## Discovery (how it connects) [#discovery-how-it-connects]

Auto-discovery via `discoverKind(root, kind)` → scans the folder map → registers by exported const name. `assembleApp(app, root)` merges additive arrays and derives page routes from relative paths (`index` dropped, `$param` → `:param`, `$` → `*`). See [Auto-Discovery](/docs/core-concepts/auto-discovery).

> \[!TIP]
> Use the generators: `kwiva make:<kind> <Name>` — 19 kinds.


# Error Handling (/docs/core-concepts/error-handling)



# Error Handling [#error-handling]

## Taxonomy [#taxonomy]

8-code enum (see [Errors](/docs/http/errors)) — `KwivaError` + subclasses.

## Helpers [#helpers]

* `error(code, msg, fields?)` — construct
* `try/catch` + rethrow

## Renderers [#renderers]

* HTTP: `toErrorResponse(error)` — auto-maps codes to status + body shape
* Client: `toClientError(status, value)` in `@kwiva/client`

## Custom codes [#custom-codes]

Extend `ErrorCode` via `KwivaError` — throw with custom messages.

## Logging [#logging]

Structured via `ctx.logger`/`createContextLogger`.

> \[!TIP]
> See [HTTP Errors](/docs/http/errors) for full taxonomy table.


# Core Concepts (/docs/core-concepts)



# Core Concepts [#core-concepts]

## Concept map [#concept-map]

```
Kwiva (framework)
├── App (defineApp)
│   ├── Models (defineModel) → Database + Migrations
│   ├── Controllers (defineController) → HTTP
│   ├── Pages (definePage) → SSR frontend
│   ├── Jobs (defineJob) → Background work
│   ├── Tasks (defineTask) → Scheduled work
│   ├── Events (defineEvent) → Pub/sub
│   ├── Middleware → HTTP pipeline
│   ├── Policies → Authorization
│   ├── Services → DI (defineService)
│   └── Config (defineConfig) → Typed sections
└── Clients, Devtools
```

| Topic                            | Page                                                  |

# Lifecycle (/docs/core-concepts/lifecycle)



# Lifecycle [#lifecycle]

## Boot [#boot]

1. `kwiva dev` / `bun src/index.ts` — entry starts server
2. `loadConfig` (src/config) + section validators
3. `configureDatabase` (database section)
4. `assembleApp` — discover + register policies
5. `createServer` + `bootApp` — mount controllers/routes/WS/OpenAPI
6. `start()`

## Request (14 steps) [#request-14-steps]

See [HTTP Lifecycle](/docs/http/lifecycle).

## Shutdown [#shutdown]

`await server.stop()` — afterResponse flush, DB close, worker stop.


# Modules (/docs/core-concepts/modules)



# Modules [#modules]

See [Modules & Plugins](/docs/modules-plugins/) — [Defining Modules](/docs/modules-plugins/defining-modules).


# Plugins (/docs/core-concepts/plugins)



# Plugins [#plugins]

See [Modules & Plugins](/docs/modules-plugins/) — [Application Composition](/docs/modules-plugins/composition).

Kwiva supports both `defineModule` and `definePlugin` via composition — modules are the primary form, plugins are lighter composites.


# Services (/docs/core-concepts/services)



# Services [#services]

`defineService(factory)` — services are just factories.

```ts title="src/app/services/notification.ts"
import { defineService } from "@kwiva/core";
import { EmailSender } from "../../app/http/controllers";

export const NotificationService = defineService(async () => {
  const sender = await EmailSender();
  return {
    async notify(msg) { await sender.send(msg); },
  };
});
```

## API [#api]

| API                                   | Notes                               |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `defineService(factory)`              | → `ServiceFactory{create(context)}` |
| `instantiateServices(factories, app)` | —                                   |

## In controllers [#in-controllers]

```ts
const notif = await instantiateServices({ NotificationService }, appCtx);
```

## DI model [#di-model]

Kwiva has a simplified DI — no class hierarchy; factories with lazy creation.


# Type Inference (/docs/core-concepts/type-inference)



# Type Inference [#type-inference]

Types derive end-to-end via route-tree:

```
Model fields → Model Definition → RouteTree
                                                  ↓
Client hooks + server handlers fully typed
```

## Examples [#examples]

```ts
const todo = await client.Todos.create({ title: "x" });
// todo: { id: number; title: string; status: "pending" | "done"; ... }
```

## `ClientRegister` [#clientregister]

Route map from `src/.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts`.


# Cache (/docs/data/cache)



# Cache [#cache]

`@kwiva/core` cache — Keyv v6 sealed backend with TTL, tags, wrap/remember (single-flight), SWR grace, tenant-aware keys.

## API [#api]

```ts
import { getCache, initCache, resetCache } from "@kwiva/core";

const cache = getCache(); // or initCache({driver: "redis", url: process.env.REDIS_URL})

await cache.set("user:1", value, { ttl: 60_000, tags: ["user"] });
await cache.get("user:1");
await cache.delete("user:1");
await cache.wrap("user:1", async () => expensive(), { ttl: 60_000 });
await cache.invalidateTags(["user"]);
```

## Config — `src/config/cache.ts` [#config--srcconfigcachets]

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  driver: "memory", // "memory" | "file" | "sqlite" | "redis" | "postgres"
  prefix: "kwiva",
  defaultTtl: 60_000, // 0 = no expiry
  tags: true, // tag-based invalidation
});
```

## Notes [#notes]

* Single-flight on `wrap` (concurrent misses share one compute).
* SWR via `CacheWrapOptions{swr?: {staleWhileRevalidate: boolean, staleWhileUpdating: boolean}}` — `staleWhileRevalidate` serves while update happens; `staleWhileUpdating` similar for updates.
* Tenant: keys prefixed via `currentTenant()` when set.

> \[!TIP]
> Model-level caching lives in `@kwiva/data` via `cache` option on models? (See advanced/model-ir note — caching is core-level; models write to `cache.wrap`.)


# Database Configuration (/docs/data/database-config)



# Database Configuration [#database-configuration]

File: `src/config/database.ts`.

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  driver: "pglite",
  // or "postgres": url / host+port+database+username+password
  pool: { max: 10, idleTimeout: 60_000, connectionTimeout: 30_000 },
  tenancy: {
    defaults: { mode: "path", tenantField: "tenant_id", models: "*", cache: { scoped: true }, storage: { scoped: true } },
  },
});
```

## Drivers [#drivers]

* `"pglite"` — in-memory PGLite (dev/test). `dataDir` for file-backed.
* `"postgres"` — real Postgres; `url` (else `DATABASE_URL`/`PG*` env), or `host/port/database/username/password`.

## Pool [#pool]

`pool: {max?, idleTimeout?, connectionTimeout?, maxLifetime?}` — all optional.

## Tenancy [#tenancy]

`TenancyConfig.defaults` — `{mode, tenantField, models, cache.scoped, storage.scoped}`.

## CLI [#cli]

`kwiva db: ...`? No — migrations only: `kwiva migrate`, `kwiva migrate:status`, `kwiva migrate:down`, `kwiva migrate:generate`, `kwiva seed`.


# Factories (/docs/data/factories)



# Factories [#factories]

```ts title="src/database/factories/post-factory.ts"
import { defineFactory } from "@kwiva/data";
import { Post } from "../models/post";

export const PostFactory = defineFactory(Post, (f) => ({
  title: `Random Post ${f.integer()}`,
}));

// in tests:
const p1 = PostFactory.make();
const many = PostFactory.makeMany(5);
const saved = await PostFactory.create();
```

Factory API: `{make, makeMany, create, createMany, resetSequences}`. Factory fields via `FactoryApi{sequence, lorem, date, uuid, pick, integer, boolean, faker-lite}`.


# Fields (/docs/data/fields)



# Fields [#fields]

`defineModel` takes `(f) => ({...})` — every value is a field builder.

## Scalar types [#scalar-types]

| Method                      | Type      | Column                |
| --------------------------- | --------- | --------------------- |
| `f.id()`                    | `id`      | `integer, primaryKey` |
| `f.uuid()`                  | `uuid`    | `uuid, primaryKey`    |
| `f.string(len?)`            | `string`  | `varchar(len=255)`    |
| `f.text()`                  | `text`    | `text`                |
| `f.integer()`, `f.bigint()` | integers  | —                     |
| `f.float()`                 | float     | —                     |
| `f.boolean()`               | bool      | —                     |
| `f.date()`, `f.time()`      | date/time | —                     |
| `f.dateTime()`              | timestamp | —                     |
| `f.json<T>()`               | json      | —                     |

## Modifiers [#modifiers]

| Method                      | Notes                                      |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `.nullable()`, `.notNull()` | nullability (default: nullable)            |
| `.indexed()`, `.unique()`   | index/unique constraint                    |
| `.default(value)`           | DB-level default                           |
| `.validation(v => v)`       | field-level validator (Error → VALIDATION) |
| `.description(text)`        | docs/openapi metadata                      |
| `.as(alias)`                | alias for SQL                              |

## Enums [#enums]

`f.enum("a", "b")` — creates a check constraint + zod/enum reflection. `enumValues` exposed on `FieldDefinition`.

## Relations [#relations]

See [Relations](/docs/data/relations).

## Query validation [#query-validation]

Relations participate in queries (`whereHas`, `withCount`); see [Relations](/docs/data/relations).

## Internal note [#internal-note]

`defineModel` compiles to core `ModelDefinition` via `compileIR`. Field kinds: `id, uuid, string, text, integer, bigint, float, boolean, date, time, dateTime, enum, json`.


# Data (/docs/data)



# Data [#data]

The data layer: models, query builder, transactions, migrations, seeders, factories.

## Layer diagram [#layer-diagram]

```
defineModel ──► Model Definition ──► model IR (ModelDefinition)
                                       ├─► @kwiva/data (queries, instance API)
                                       ├─► schema → migrations
                                       ├─► @kwiva/http (REST + auto-routes)
                                       ├─► @kwiva/client (typed client)
                                       ├─► @kwiva/mcp (tools, list/get/create/update/delete)
                                       └─► @kwiva/search (FTS)
```

## Entry points [#entry-points]

| Topic                                                              | Page                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Models (defineModel)                                               | [Models](/docs/data/models)                          |
| Field DSL (id/string/enum/json/belongsTo...)                       | [Fields](/docs/data/fields)                          |
| Relations (belongsTo, hasMany, hasOne, manyToMany, through, morph) | [Relations](/docs/data/relations)                    |
| Validation (Standard Schema, field DSL)                            | [Validation](/docs/data/validation)                  |
| Query builder                                                      | [Queries](/docs/data/queries)                        |
| Pagination                                                         | [Pagination](/docs/data/pagination)                  |
| Transactions                                                       | [Transactions](/docs/data/transactions)              |
| Migrations                                                         | [Migrations](/docs/data/migrations)                  |
| Seeders                                                            | [Seeders](/docs/data/seeders)                        |
| Factories                                                          | [Factories](/docs/data/factories)                    |
| Soft deletes                                                       | [Soft Deletes](/docs/data/soft-deletes)              |
| DB config (`database` section)                                     | [Database Configuration](/docs/data/database-config) |
| Storage (disks, uploads, signed URLs, fakes)                       | [File Storage](/docs/data/storage)                   |
| Cache (Keyv v6)                                                    | [Cache & KV](/docs/data/cache)                       |
| Search (Postgres FTS, searchAcross)                                | [Search](/docs/data/search)                          |

## Key concepts [#key-concepts]

* **Model as source of truth**: one `defineModel` feeds schema, migrations, REST, typed client, MCP, audit — no drift.
* **Fluent instance API**: `save/update/delete/restore/refresh`, `toJSON`, `isDirty`, `getOriginal`.
* **Global scopes**: attach with `scope()` — applies to every query unless opted out.
* **Tenancy**: automatic query scoping via `tenancy` section + ALS scopes.


# Migrations (/docs/data/migrations)



# Migrations [#migrations]

Kwiva uses **schema-diff driven migrations**: the model IR is the source of truth; `kwiva migrate` diffs models against the live DB.

## `defineMigration` [#definemigration]

```ts title="src/database/migrations/20260101000000_create_posts.ts"
import { defineMigration } from "@kwiva/data";

export const CreatePosts = defineMigration("20260101000000_create_posts", (db) =>
  db.createTable("posts", (t) => {
    t.id();
    t.string("title").nullable(false);
    t.dateTime("createdAt").notNull().defaultNow();
  }),
);
```

`Migration` struct: `{name, up, down?}` — timestamped names (`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_*`); rollback to last batch; migrations without `down` throw on `migrate:down`.

## CLI commands [#cli-commands]

| Command                  | Purpose                                                       |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kwiva migrate`          | apply all migrations in order                                 |
| `kwiva migrate:status`   | `applied: ...` / `pending: ...`                               |
| `kwiva migrate:down`     | roll back last batch                                          |
| `kwiva migrate:generate` | generate diffs from model IR (drift → `operations`, `source`) |

`migrateGenerate(models, db?)` returns `{operations, source, extra}`.

## Searchable migrations [#searchable-migrations]

`db.searchable()` — writes FTS triggers + index for `@kwiva/search`.

## Custom Migrations [#custom-migrations]

Full `MigrationSchema`: `createTable, addColumn, dropTable, addIndex, dropColumn, addComment, searchable`. Type exports: `TableBuilder, ColumnBuilder, ColumnTypeBuilder, DdlOp...`.


# Models (/docs/data/models)



# Models [#models]

```ts title="src/app/models/post.ts"
import { defineModel } from "@kwiva/data";

export const Post = defineModel("posts", (f) => ({
  id: f.id(),
  title: f.string(),
  status: f.enum("draft", "published"),
  author: f.belongsTo(() => User),
  tags: f.manyToMany(() => Tag),
}), {
  timestamps: true,
  routes: true,
  fillable: ["title", "status"],
  hidden: ["password"],
  permission: "posts",
});
```

## Options [#options]

| Option                 | Type                                      | Notes                                                                                                                                |
