| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `timestamps`           | bool                                      | adds `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (or provided names)                                                                                     |
| `softDelete`           | bool                                      | adds `deletedAt`                                                                                                                     |
| `audit`                | bool                                      | adds `createdBy`/`updatedBy` (uses `ctx.user.id`)                                                                                    |
| `tenantField`          | string                                    | auto-scopes this model by current tenant                                                                                             |
| `permission`           | string                                    | permission namespace (gates generated routes)                                                                                        |
| `fillable` / `guarded` | string\[]                                 | write whitelist/blacklist                                                                                                            |
| `hidden` / `visible`   | string\[]                                 | toJSON serialization                                                                                                                 |
| `routes`               | bool                                      | generate 5 REST routes                                                                                                               |
| `primaryKey`           | string                                    | override default `id`                                                                                                                |
| `hooks`                | object                                    | `beforeCreate`, `afterCreate`, `beforeSave`, `beforeUpdate`, `afterUpdate`, `beforeDelete`, `afterDelete`, `beforeFind`, `afterFind` |
| `indexes`              | array                                     | `[{columns, unique?, name?}]`                                                                                                        |
| `uniques`              | array                                     | composite unique constraints                                                                                                         |
| `search`               | `{fields: [{field, weight?}], language?}` | enables Postgres FTS on this model                                                                                                   |

## Field DSL [#field-dsl]

See [Fields](/docs/data/fields). Types: `id, uuid, string, text, integer, bigint, float, boolean, date, dateTime, time, enum, json, belongsTo, hasOne, hasMany, manyToMany, hasOneThrough, hasManyThrough, morphTo, morphMany, morphToMany`.

## Instance API [#instance-api]

| Member                                                                            | Notes                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `model.save()`                                                                    | insert or update (not-null check via `id`) |
| `model.update(data)`                                                              | —                                          |
| `model.delete()`                                                                  | (soft delete if enabled)                   |
| `model.forceDelete()`, `model.restore()`, `model.trashed`                         | soft-delete API                            |
| `model.refresh()`                                                                 | reload from DB                             |
| `model.replicate(except?)`                                                        | clone → new instance                       |
| `model.loadMissing(rel)`, `model.associate(rel, id)`, `model.dissociate(rel)`     | relations                                  |
| `model.isDirty`, `model.isClean`, `model.wasChanged`, `model.getOriginal(field?)` | change tracking                            |
| `model.toJSON()`                                                                  | —                                          |

## Generated REST surface [#generated-rest-surface]

```plaintext
GET    /api/{model}         list (validated where/page/orderBy/with)
GET    /api/{model}/:id     get
POST   /api/{model}         create (validated)
PATCH  /api/{model}/:id     update
DELETE /api/{model}/:id     remove
```

> \[!TIP]
> FTS search: `Post.search("term", {includeRank: true})` — see [Search](/docs/data/search).


# Pagination (/docs/data/pagination)



# Pagination [#pagination]

Two strategies: offset (`page(page, perPage)`) and cursor (`cursor(col, table, limit)`).

## Offset pagination [#offset-pagination]

```ts
await Post.page(1, { size: 20 }).where("status", "=", "published").orderBy("id", "desc").all();
```

Response: `{ items, page, size, total, pages }`.

## Cursor pagination [#cursor-pagination]

```ts
await Post.cursor("id", "posts", { limit: 50 }).all();
```

Response: `{ items, cursor, hasMore }` (stable keysets; use unique col, e.g. `id` or `createdAt`).

## Config (`src/config/app.ts` or similar) [#config-srcconfigappts-or-similar]

```ts
export default defineConfig({ defaultPerPage: 20, maxPerPage: 100 });
```

## Client side [#client-side]

`useInfiniteList` hooks handle both automatically.


# Queries (/docs/data/queries)



# Queries [#queries]

`Model.query()` (via `Model.<method>` static methods or `QueryBuilder`).

## Common builders [#common-builders]

| API                                                 | Notes                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.where(col, op, value)` / `.where(col, value)`     | operator forms: `=, !=, >, <, >=, <=, like, ilike, in, notIn, between, is, isNot` |
| `.orWhere(...)`                                     | —                                                                                 |
| `.whereIn(col, arr)`                                | —                                                                                 |
| `.whereNull(col)` / `.whereNotNull(col)`            | —                                                                                 |
| `.orderBy(col, "asc"/"desc")` / `.orderByDesc(col)` | —                                                                                 |
| `.limit(n)` / `.offset(n)`                          | —                                                                                 |
| `.select(...cols)`                                  | —                                                                                 |
| `.with("relation")`                                 | eager load (see [Relations](/docs/data/relations))                                |
| `.having(col, op, value)`                           | aggregates with groups                                                            |
| `.useCursor()`                                      | —                                                                                 |
| `.useLocks()`                                       | `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`                                                           |

## Terminals [#terminals]

| API                                                                                                               | Notes      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `.get()`, `.all()`, `.first()`, `.firstOrFail()`, `.firstOrNull()`, `.firstOrCreate(where)`, `.firstOrNew(where)` | —          |
| `.value(col)`, `.pluck(col)`                                                                                      | —          |
| `.count()`, `.max(col)`, `.min(col)`, `.avg(col)`, `.sum(col)`                                                    | aggregates |
| `.chunk(n)`, `.chunkById(n, col)`                                                                                 | streaming  |

## Transactions [#transactions]

```ts
await db.transaction(async (tx) => {
  // tx.execute / tx.insert etc.
});
```

## `db` access [#db-access]

```ts
import { db } from "@kwiva/data";
db.execute(sql`SELECT ...`); // from core?
```

See [Transactions](/docs/data/transactions) for `db`, `upsert`, savepoints.


# Relations (/docs/data/relations)



# Relations [#relations]

```ts title="src/app/models/post.ts"
import { defineModel } from "@kwiva/data";

export const Post = defineModel("posts", (f) => ({
  id: f.id(),
  title: f.string(),
  author: f.belongsTo(() => User),
  comments: f.hasMany(() => Comment),
  subscribers: f.manyToMany(() => Subscriber),
  // through
  teamMembers: f.hasManyThrough(() => Member, () => PostToOrg),
  // polymorphic
  attachment: f.morphTo(),
}));
```

## Relation kinds (10) [#relation-kinds-10]

| Kind                               | Signature                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `belongsTo`                        | one FK column + join via `foreignKey`/`localKey`                                          |
| `hasOne`                           | reverse belongsTo (one record)                                                            |
| `hasMany`                          | reverse belongsTo (many)                                                                  |
| `manyToMany`                       | pivot via `manyToMany(target, {through: Pivot})` or automatic pivot (`posts_subscribers`) |
| `hasOneThrough` / `hasManyThrough` | via intermediate model                                                                    |
| `morphTo` / `morphMany`            | `polymorphic, name`, target optional                                                      |
| `morphToMany`                      | polymorphic many-to-many                                                                  |

## Modifiers [#modifiers]

* `.optional()` — for nullable relations

## Querying [#querying]

| API                                                                       | Notes                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `Post.with("comments")`                                                   | eager load                     |
| `Post.has("comments")` / `Post.whereHas("comments", (q) => q.where(...))` | constraint filtering           |
| `Post.withCount("comments")`                                              | add `comments_count`           |
| `Post.withAggregate("comments", "sum", "likes")`                          | `sum/min/max/avg`              |
| `Post.whereDoesntHave("comments")`                                        | inverse of whereHas            |
| `instance.loadMissing("author")`                                          | lazy load if not loaded        |
| `instance.author`                                                         | relation handles: `{ load() }` |

## Auto-pivot (manyToMany) [#auto-pivot-manytomany]

`f.manyToMany(() => Subscriber)` — Kwiva derives the pivot table (`<model>_<other>`) via `kwiva db diff` — appears in `src/database/migrations/`.

## Examples [#examples]

```ts
const post = await Post.whereHas("comments", (q) =>
  q.where("text", "ilike", "%broken%"),
).withCount("comments").first();
```


# Search (/docs/data/search)



# Search [#search]

`@kwiva/search` — Postgres full-text search over model IR.

## Model config [#model-config]

```ts title="src/app/models/post.ts"
import { defineModel } from "@kwiva/data";

export const Post = defineModel("posts", (f) => ({
  id: f.id(),
  title: f.string(),
  body: f.text(),
}), {
  search: {
    fields: [{ field: "title", weight: "A" }, { field: "body", weight: "B" }],
    language: "english", // regconfig-style Postgres FTS config
  },
});
```

## Query-time search [#query-time-search]

```ts
const { items, total } = await Post.search("github", { includeRank: true }).limit(20).all();
// items[i].__searchRank — ts_rank-like score
```

## Reindex [#reindex]

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva search:reindex        # all searchable models
kwiva search:reindex Post   # one
```

## Federated search [#federated-search]

```ts
import { searchAcross } from "@kwiva/search";
const hits = await searchAcross([Post, Comment], "deploy", 10);
// hits: [{model, row, rank}]
```

## Config — `src/config/search.ts` [#config--srcconfigsearchts]

```ts
export default defineConfig({ engine: "postgres", language: "english" });
```


# Seeders (/docs/data/seeders)



# Seeders [#seeders]

```ts title="src/database/seeders/posts-seed.ts"
import { defineSeeder, seed } from "@kwiva/data";
import { Post } from "@kwiva/data";

export const SeedPosts = defineSeeder(async ({ db }) => {
  await seed([{ key: "hello", value: { title: "Hello" } }], {
    // or upsert into Post
    Post: [{ id: 1, title: "Hello", status: "draft" }],
  });
});
```

`defineSeeder(handler: (ctx: SeederContext{db}) => void | Promise<void>)` — runs in order; `seed(entries, only?)` — idempotent.

CLI: `kwiva seed`, `kwiva seed <name>`.


# Soft Deletes (/docs/data/soft-deletes)



# Soft Deletes [#soft-deletes]

```ts title="src/app/models/post.ts"
import { defineModel } from "@kwiva/data";
export const Post = defineModel("posts", (f) => ({
  id: f.id(),
  title: f.string(),
}), { softDelete: true });
```

Add `deletedAt` column. APIs on instances: `delete()` → sets `deletedAt`; `restore()`; `forceDelete()`; `withTrashed()`, `onlyTrashed()`, `trashed` flag.

Query side: default queries exclude trashed; `model.withTrashed()`, `.onlyTrashed()`.


# File Storage (/docs/data/storage)



# File Storage [#file-storage]

`@kwiva/storage` — S3-compatible disks API over Files SDK (sealed engine).

## Config — `src/config/storage.ts` [#config--srcconfigstoragets]

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  default: "local",
  disks: {
    local: { driver: "local", root: "./storage/app", publicUrl: null },
    s3: { driver: "s3", options: { bucket, region, prefix: "uploads" } },
  },
  tenant: { scoped: true, prefix: "tenants" },
});
```

Drivers: `"local" | "memory" | "s3" | "gcs" | "azure" | "vercel-blob"` (STORAGE\_DRIVERS).

## Storage facade [#storage-facade]

```ts
import { storage } from "@kwiva/storage";

await storage.put("avatar.png", file.arrayBuffer(), { contentType: "image/png" });
const data = await storage.get("avatar.png");
await storage.delete("avatar.png");
await storage.list({ prefix: "uploads" });
```

## Disk (tenant-scoped) [#disk-tenant-scoped]

`storage.disk("local")` — same API. `storage.disk("s3").file("a.txt").url()` — public URL helper.

## Signed URLs [#signed-urls]

* `storage.signedUrl("file.pdf", { expiresIn: 60_000 })` — GET url
* `storage.signedUploadUrl("uploads/x.bin", { expiresIn: 60_000, contentType })` — returns `{url, method, headers?}`

## Assets (hashed manifest) [#assets-hashed-manifest]

`assetUrl("./my.svg", { baseUrl })` — resolves via `public/assets-manifest.json` or `KWIVA_ASSET_MANIFEST`.

## Fakes (tests) [#fakes-tests]

```ts
const fake = storage.fake();
fake.assertUploaded(disk, key);
fake.assertMissing(disk, key);
```

## Errors [#errors]

`StorageError` codes: `STORAGE_NOT_FOUND`, `STORAGE_CONFLICT`, `STORAGE_INVALID`, `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`, `STORAGE_TENANT_REQUIRED`.


# Transactions (/docs/data/transactions)



# Transactions [#transactions]

```ts
import { db } from "@kwiva/data";

await db.transaction(async () => {
  await Post.create({ title: "x" });
  await db.execute("UPDATE counters SET n = n + 1");
});
```

## Nested transactions (savepoints) [#nested-transactions-savepoints]

Inner `db.transaction` → SAVEPOINT; inner failure rolls back to savepoint (outer continues).

## Transactional outbox (for events/jobs) [#transactional-outbox-for-eventsjobs]

```ts
// inside a transaction:
import { enqueueOutbox } from "@kwiva/jobs";
await enqueueOutbox(SendWelcomeJob, { userId: 1 });

// inside the same tx:
import { enqueueOutbox as enqueueEvent } from "@kwiva/events"; // broadcast metadata + outbox
await enqueueEvent(UserSignedUp, { id: 1 });

// after commit:
drainOutbox(); // dispatches from outbox
```

> \[!TIP]
> See [Events → broadcast metadata](/docs/realtime/events) and [@kwiva/jobs outbox](/api/jobs#outbox).


# Validation (/docs/data/validation)



# Validation [#validation]

## 1. Field DSL validation (write-time) [#1-field-dsl-validation-write-time]

Fields with `.validation(v => v)` use Standard Schema (`@standard-schema/utils`). Issues → `ValidationError` with `fields: Record<string, string[]>`.

```ts title="src/app/models/post.ts"
export const Post = defineModel("posts", (f) => ({
  title: f.string().validation((s) => s.min(1).max(200)),
  email: f.string().validation((v) => (v.trim() ? true : "email is required")),
}));
```

## 2. Route-level validation (input) [#2-route-level-validation-input]

Every route input entry is validated via Standard Schema (params, query, body, headers, cookies).

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/posts.ts"
api.post("/", handler, {
  input: { body: CreatePostBody },
  // or query/params/headers/cookie entries
});
```

## 3. Contracts [#3-contracts]

`defineContract({request, response})` — typed, generated OpenAPI + zod validation.

## Error shape [#error-shape]

```json title="422 response"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION",
    "message": "Invalid input",
    "fields": { "body.title": ["Too short"], "body.email": ["Required"] },
    "requestId": "req_abc123"
  }
}
```

> \[!TIP]
> Validation runs before middleware on write paths; GET-side validation on query/params.


# Runtime Adapters (/docs/deployment/adapters)



# Runtime Adapters [#runtime-adapters]

## Concepts [#concepts]

* **Adapters** — `getElysia(server)` returns an Elysia instance tuned per runtime.
* **Presets** — deployment presets for major targets.
* Target: Bun (primary), Node, serverless (API-only), containers.

## Usage [#usage]

No adapter config needed for default targets.

```ts
// src/index.ts (app entry — kwiva dev uses this)
export default await createServer({ port: 3000 }).start();
```

## Platform targets [#platform-targets]

| Platform              | Target shape                                              | Notes         |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Node/Bun (standalone) | `bun dist/index.js` or `bun start`                        | primary       |
| Docker/Kubernetes     | `bun src/index.ts` + Dockerfile                           | containers    |
| Vercel/Netlify        | serverless                                                | API-only mode |
| Cloudflare Workers    | via user wrapper (custom integration — see research gaps) | —             |

## Supported platforms [#supported-platforms]

* Local (Windows/macOS/Linux)
* VPS/bare-metal
* Docker/K8s
* Node + Bun standalone

Serverless in principle via adapters.


# Container Deployment (/docs/deployment/containers)



# Container Deployment [#container-deployment]

## Dockerfile (Node/Bun base) [#dockerfile-nodebun-base]

```dockerfile
FROM oven/bun:1.4
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
RUN bun install
RUN bun run build
EXPOSE 3000
ENV PORT=3000
CMD ["bun", "dist/index.js"]
```

## Migrations on boot [#migrations-on-boot]

Container startup runs `kwiva migrate` before starting server.

## Stateless rules [#stateless-rules]

* External DB (Postgres)
* External cache (Redis/postgres)
* External jobs (pg-boss or memory queue + scheduler)

## Scaling [#scaling]

* Multi-replica via load balancer; Kwiva is stateless by default
* Shared stores required for chat/presence

> \[!TIP]
> Common pitfall: keeping in-memory jobs — they won't persist.


# Deployment (/docs/deployment)



# Deployment [#deployment]

Kwiva is a build-time-only deploy: `kwiva build` produces `dist/`; deploy that. One codebase for Bun/Node/serverless/containers.

## Entry points [#entry-points]

| Topic                 | Page                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Runtime Adapters      | [Runtime Adapters](/docs/deployment/adapters)                 |
| Node/Bun Deployment   | [Node/Bun Deployment](/docs/deployment/node-bun)              |
| Serverless Deployment | [Serverless Deployment](/docs/deployment/serverless)          |
| Container Deployment  | [Container Deployment](/docs/deployment/containers)           |
| Production Checklist  | [Production Checklist](/docs/deployment/production-checklist) |

## TL;DR [#tldr]

```bash title="terminal"
bun run install
kwiva build --out .output
# then: bun ./dist/index.js (or node for Node targets)
```

> \[!TIP]
> For a VPS, use [Node/Bun Deployment](/docs/deployment/node-bun); for cloud, [Runtime Adapters](/docs/deployment/adapters).


# Node/Bun Deployment (/docs/deployment/node-bun)



# Node/Bun Deployment [#nodebun-deployment]

## Default entry [#default-entry]

`src/index.ts` — main entry that starts the app server on port 3000.

## Run [#run]

```bash title="terminal"
# Bun
bun dist/index.js

# Node (ESM)
node dist/index.js
```

## Environment [#environment]

* `PORT` — default 3000
* `APP_KEY` — required
* `AUTH_SESSION_SECRET` — from `defineConfig` auth
* `BASE_URL` — via `env()` config or CLI

## Health [#health]

`GET /api/health` — framework endpoint.

## Process management [#process-management]

Use systemd/supervisor; Kwiva has no built-in supervisor.

## Notes [#notes]

* Bun is primary: `bun --version >= 1.4.0`
* Node compatible for API-only
* `ENGINE=bun` — primary. Node-only for API deployments.


# Production Checklist (/docs/deployment/production-checklist)



# Production Checklist [#production-checklist]

Before deploying:

* [ ] `APP_KEY` set (`kwiva key:generate`)
* [ ] `AUTH_SESSION_SECRET` set (non-empty)
* [ ] `kwiva migrate` applied
* [ ] `kwiva seed` for dev data (if needed)
* [ ] `storage` configured with real disks
* [ ] TLS via reverse proxy
* [ ] Rate limiting on public routes (`cors/csrf/rateLimit`)
* [ ] Observability on (logging/tracing)
* [ ] Health check: `GET /api/health`
* [ ] One replica + health checks

See also [Security → Production](/docs/security/production).


# Serverless Deployment (/docs/deployment/serverless)



# Serverless Deployment [#serverless-deployment]

Kwiva supports serverless deployment via runtime adapters:

* AWS Lambda
* Vercel Functions (JS runtime)
* Cloudflare Workers (custom adapter — see research gaps, planned)

## Constraints [#constraints]

* Apps run stateless; external DB (Postgres) recommended
* No long-running dev-mode jobs; use queues + workers
* Streaming SSE limited by platform timeouts

## Setup [#setup]

Wrap `createServer().handle(request)` in your platform adapter.

> \[!TIP]
> `getElysia(server)` abstracts HTTP layer for all adapters.


# Data Hooks (/docs/frontend/data-hooks)



# Data Hooks [#data-hooks]

From `@kwiva/client` — TanStack Query based.

## Hooks [#hooks]

| Hook                                        | Purpose                            |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `useResource(routeId, args?, options?)`     | generic query                      |
| `useList(routeId, args?, options?)`         | list queries                       |
| `useMutation(routeId, options?)`            | mutations (with auto-invalidation) |
| `useUpload(routeId, options?)`              | file upload mutations              |
| `useInfiniteList(routeId, args?, options?)` | infinite scroll                    |
| `useForm(initial, options?)`                | form state + submit                |
| `connectRoute(routeId, args?, opts?)`       | WS connection                      |

## Mutations [#mutations]

```ts
const [mutate, state] = useMutation("TodosController.create");
await mutate({ title: "Buy milk" });
```

## Invalidation [#invalidation]

`routeFamily("TodosController.list")` — returns the family for auto-invalidation.

## Cache [#cache]

`enableCachePersistence({storage, key, maxAge})` — persisted QueryClient cache.

## QueryClient [#queryclient]

`createQueryClient()`, `getQueryClient()`, `resetQueryClient()`, `dehydrateClient(client)`, `ClientProvider({children, client?, dehydratedState?})`.

## Optimistic updates (M2+) [#optimistic-updates-m2]

Use `useMutation` + `queryClient.setQueryData` patterns — via typed routes.

> \[!TIP]
> For SSR-safe cache transfer, see [Cache & KV](/docs/data/cache).


# Frontend (/docs/frontend)



The frontend is a first-class, fully owned part of the framework. Pages, routing, layouts, loaders, data hooks, the typed RPC client, and the built-in UI kit are all part of the same `defineX` surface — one cohesive narrative instead of a stack of stitched-together libraries. Routing decisions are locked by the framework's ADRs (ADR-0005 owns the router, ADR-0006 owns SSR orchestration), so the engineering ergonomics of the reference router are implemented natively — without the dependency or the version pin.

By default every page is **server-rendered**. Loaders run on the server, the first paint arrives as HTML, and hydration transfers the loaded data into the client-side data-hook cache without a refetch. The exact same `definePage` files can run as a client-rendered single-page application in `api+spa` mode — the page code does not change. Rendering is a framework responsibility, not an add-on.

## The Full-Stack Loop [#the-full-stack-loop]

The frontend sits at the end of a loop that starts in the data layer:

```plaintext title="the-full-stack-loop.txt"
defineModel → defineController → @kwiva/client → definePage loader → data hooks
```

A model declared once with `defineModel` produces its API. Controllers shape those endpoints and add custom actions. The typed client derives its call signatures from the same route manifest. Page loaders call that client. Data hooks consume the loader's results from the same cache. One type universe flows through the entire loop with **zero code generation** — types are derived at type level from the route manifest and the model IR.

The practical effect is that params, search state, loader data, and mutations are all checked at the call site. A page that reads `params.id` and calls `client.posts.get(params.id)` is validated against the real route file and the real controller before it ever ships. Loaders are lint-gated to the typed client (`no-raw-fetch-in-loaders`), so the loop cannot be bypassed by a stray `fetch`.

## Ownership: Four Packages [#ownership-four-packages]

The frontend is split across four packages, each with a narrow job:

| Package         | Role                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@kwiva/react`  | Page and component bindings — `definePage`, `Providers`, data hooks, navigation hooks |
| `@kwiva/router` | The owned router core — route tree, matching, loaders, guards, history                |
| `@kwiva/client` | The typed RPC client — end-to-end typed calls, SSR-safe, session-aware                |
| `@kwiva/ui-kit` | The component layer — tokens, primitives, components, and whole-screen patterns       |

The router core is runtime-agnostic; `@kwiva/react` binds it to pages and components. The client is used by both, which is why the same call surface works in loaders, hooks, and tests. The UI kit is the only fully replaceable layer — apps may keep it, swap it, or render plain utility-first CSS, provided they maintain the token surface the Studio uses.

## What the Frontend Includes [#what-the-frontend-includes]

| Topic                                          | What it covers                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Pages](/docs/frontend/pages)                  | `definePage` — the factory for every page: validation, loader, guards, pending/error/not-found UI, head meta, component |
| [File-Based Routing](/docs/frontend/routing)   | The `src/ui/pages/**` file tree, dynamic segments, splats, nested folders, route context                                |
| [Nested Layouts](/docs/frontend/layouts)       | `__root.tsx`, folder layout files, layout composition, layout-level loaders                                             |
| [Loaders & Data](/docs/frontend/loaders)       | Parallel and streamed loaders, deferred data with `stream()`, `beforeLoad` guards, loader hydration                     |
| [Navigation & Link](/docs/frontend/navigation) | Typed `Link`, programmatic navigation, intent preloading, scroll restoration                                            |
| [Data Hooks](/docs/frontend/data-hooks)        | `useResource`, `useList`, `useMutation`, `useInfiniteList`, invalidation, suspense                                      |
| [RPC Client](/docs/frontend/rpc-client)        | `createClient`, end-to-end typed calls, SSR-safe dedupe, subscriptions, testing                                         |
| [UI Components](/docs/frontend/ui-components)  | The built-in UI kit — layout primitives, `Link`, form primitives, Studio screens                                        |

Each page walks one surface in full and cross-links the others, so the set reads as a single reference rather than overlapping tutorials.

## Server-Rendered by Default [#server-rendered-by-default]

Every page participates in the framework-owned rendering pipeline by default:

```plaintext title="server-rendered-by-default.txt"
request (page route)
  → router match (owned router)
  → beforeLoad guards (session → login redirects)
  → loaders execute in parallel (server-side, via the typed client, in-process)
  → suspense-aware HTML streaming
  → response stream (status, headers, cookies from the pipeline)
hydration (client)
  → state rehydrates into the data-hook cache (no refetch of loader data)
  → router picks up at the same route with the same search state
```

Route rules let you choose — per path — whether the response is dynamically rendered, cached for a window, revalidated, or prerendered at build time. See [Rendering](/docs/rendering) for the full pipeline and its knobs, [Loaders & Data](/docs/frontend/loaders) for the server-side data pass, and [Pages](/docs/frontend/pages) for the full `definePage` contract.

## Runtime Selection [#runtime-selection]

React is the default runtime, selected once in UI configuration:

```ts title="src/config/ui.ts"
// src/config/ui.ts
export default defineConfig('ui', {
  defaults: { runtime: 'react', theme: 'kwiva' },
})
```

`runtime: 'compact'` swaps in the compact runtime at build time via the framework's own transform — one config flip, mostly smaller bundles, and application code unchanged. Hydration semantics, the data-hook cache, and the render pipeline are identical across runtimes. See [Hydration](/docs/rendering/hydration) for the shared contract.

## One Cache, Client and Server [#one-cache-client-and-server]

Loaders and data hooks read and write the same cache. When a loader runs on the server, its results dehydrate into the page stream; on the client they rehydrate into the data-hook cache under identical keys. Navigation reuses what is already present — there is no double fetch between navigate and render. Intent preloading populates that same cache, so hovering a link warms the data the next page is about to render.

Keys are derived from **model identity plus arguments**, never hand-built. `invalidate(Post)` clears every list, detail, and custom entry touching the `Post` model; `invalidateTags([...])` clears route-rule caches on the server. Client freshness and server responses stay consistent because both read from one contract. See [Data Hooks](/docs/frontend/data-hooks) and [Caching Strategies](/docs/rendering/caching).

## Generated Types, No Codegen [#generated-types-no-codegen]

The route tree, its params, its search schemas, and its loader return types are compiled into generated types under `src/.kwiva/types`. The framework reads these at type level — there is no runtime codegen step, no build-time code generation, and nothing to commit. The same generated surface powers `Route.useParams()`, `Route.useSearch()`, `Route.useLoaderData()`, typed `<Link>` targets, and navigation calls. Invalid `to`, `params`, or `search` values fail **at compile time** — a broken link is a type error, not a 404 at runtime. See [File-Based Routing](/docs/frontend/routing) for the type-generation pipeline.

## Getting Started [#getting-started]

Page files are discovered by convention, so there is nothing to register: drop `index.tsx` into `src/ui/pages/` and the `/` route exists. Generate a typed scaffold with the CLI:

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva make:page posts.$id
```

The scaffold ships a typed stub with the provider tree, a loader wired to the typed client, and the streaming suspension points in place. [Your First Page](/docs/getting-started/first-page) walks a page end to end, and [CLI Generators](/docs/cli/generators) lists the scaffold commands.

## Server and Client Execution [#server-and-client-execution]

`definePage` files execute in two contexts, and both are first-class. On the server, loaders run in-process with the full request context — session, tenant, and config are the same objects HTTP handlers see, so a page can never render past an authorization boundary. On the client, the same loader runs with the provider-resolved context during navigation, and its result lands in the identical cache keys. Single-page mode is a projection of the same files, not a rewrite. See [SSR](/docs/rendering/ssr) and [Hydration](/docs/rendering/hydration).

## Development Experience [#development-experience]

The dev side is part of the frontend, not an afterthought:

* The dev overlay lists the route tree, loader timings, and cache state (v1.x)
* Loader waterfalls and OTel trace ids attach to each request's rendering stages
* `kwiva make:page posts.$id` scaffolds a full typed page in one command
* Hydration problems surface as cache-key diagnostics, not silent mismatches

See [Observability: Dev Overlay](/docs/observability/dev-overlay) for the overlay and [CLI Generators](/docs/cli/generators) for scaffolds.

## What's Next [#whats-next]

1. [Pages](/docs/frontend/pages) — start with the `definePage` contract
2. [File-Based Routing](/docs/frontend/routing) — how files become routes
3. [Loaders & Data](/docs/frontend/loaders) — getting data into pages
4. [Data Hooks](/docs/frontend/data-hooks) — client-side data access
5. [Rendering](/docs/rendering) — SSR, streaming, and hydration


# Layouts (/docs/frontend/layouts)



# Layouts [#layouts]

`src/ui/layouts/**` — recursive; every page gets root layout first.

## `layoutSegments(relativePath)` [#layoutsegmentsrelativepath]

| File                        | Segments                    |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `root.tsx`                  | `[]` (root)                 |
| `admin/index.tsx`           | `["admin"]`                 |
| `admin/todos/[id]/root.tsx` | `["admin", "todos", ":id"]` |

## `layoutComponent(module, displayPath)` — → `LayoutComponent` [#layoutcomponentmodule-displaypath---layoutcomponent]

## `resolveLayouts(pathname, layouts)` [#resolvelayoutspathname-layouts]

Shallowest-first; page wraps everything (deepest wraps page first).

## Layout file shape [#layout-file-shape]

```tsx
import { layoutSegments } from "@kwiva/ui";
export default function AdminLayout({ children }) {
  return <div className="admin">{children}</div>;
}
```

> \[!TIP]
> Custom layouts via `File`/`Folder`/`Files` MDX components in docs.


# Loaders (/docs/frontend/loaders)



# Loaders [#loaders]

`definePage` has `load(ctx)` — the loader.

## Loader API [#loader-api]

* `ctx.params` / `ctx.query`
* `ctx.waitUntil(promise)` — defer until response sent
* Deps via `loaderDeps` — n/a for Kwiva (caching per request)

## Streaming [#streaming]

`streamPage` for partial HTML with Suspense; defer via `defer()` segments.

## Example [#example]

```tsx
export default definePage({
  load(ctx) {
    return { id: ctx.params.id };
  },
  render({ props, ctx }) {
    return <article>{props.id}</article>;
  },
});
```

> \[!TIP]
> Loaders are awaited (no async iterator today); see [Streaming SSR](/docs/rendering/streaming).


# Navigation (/docs/frontend/navigation)



# Navigation [#navigation]

## `Link` (soft navigation) [#link-soft-navigation]

```tsx
import { Link } from "@kwiva/ui";
<Link href="/about" prefetch={true}>About</Link>
```

## `useRouter` — `visit(url, {replace?, preserveState?})`, `reload()`, `back()`, `on("start"|"finish"|"error")` [#userouter--visiturl-replace-preservestate-reload-back-onstartfinisherror]

## `usePage` — `{url, component, props, session}` [#usepage--url-component-props-session]

## `hydrateApp({pages, layouts?, events?})` — hydrate on client load [#hydrateapppages-layouts-events--hydrate-on-client-load]

## Prefetch [#prefetch]

`setLinkPrefetcher(fn)` — custom fetcher for prefetches (via fetchEnvelope).

## Scroll restoration [#scroll-restoration]

`installScrollRestoration(events, options?)` → disposer.

> \[!TIP]
> `fetchEnvelope(url)` returns `{component, url, props}` for soft-nav assets.


# Pages (/docs/frontend/pages)



# Pages [#pages]

```ts title="src/ui/pages/todos.$id.tsx"
import { definePage } from "@kwiva/ui";

export default definePage({
  load(ctx) {
    return { id: ctx.params.id };
  },
  render({ props }) {
    return <main>Todo #{props.id}</main>;
  },
  head() {
    return { title: `Todo #${props.id}` };
  },
});
```

## DefinePage contract [#definepage-contract]

| Field           | Type                           | Notes                                                  |
| --------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `path`          | string                         | for the `(path, options)` form                         |
| `load(ctx)`     | `(ctx: HttpContext) => object` | server-side, streamed with SSR                         |
| `render(props)` | ReactElement                   | —                                                      |
| `head()`        | `PageHead`                     | `{title?, meta?, link?, canonical?, jsonLd?, robots?}` |
| `middleware`    | `Middleware[]`                 | —                                                      |

## Head options (`PageHead`) [#head-options-pagehead]

| Field       | Notes                    |
| ----------- | ------------------------ |
| `title`     | —                        |
| `meta`      | `{name?, content?}[]`    |
| `link`      | `{rel, href}[]`          |
| `canonical` | —                        |
| `jsonLd`    | JSON-LD structured data  |
| `robots`    | `robots.txt`-style rules |

## Discovery [#discovery]

Pages are discovered recursively from `src/ui/pages/**` via `pagesFromRegistry`; `derivePageRoute` maps file → route (`index.tsx` → root, `$id` → `:id`, `$` → `*`).

## `streamPage(options)` [#streampageoptions]

Streaming SSR variant: `{head, tree, seed, clientScript, extraScripts?}`.

## NotFound/Redirect [#notfoundredirect]

`redirect(path, status?)`, `notFound()` throw special classes handled by SSR.


# File-Based Routing (/docs/frontend/routing)



# File-Based Routing [#file-based-routing]

Routes derive from file paths in `src/ui/pages/**`.

## Route map [#route-map]

| File                           | Route         |
| ------------------------------ | ------------- |
| `src/ui/pages/index.tsx`       | `/`           |
| `src/ui/pages/about.tsx`       | `/about`      |
| `src/ui/pages/todos.$id.tsx`   | `/todos/:id`  |
| `src/ui/pages/todos/index.tsx` | `/todos`      |
| `src/ui/pages/blog/$slug.tsx`  | `/blog/:slug` |
| `src/ui/pages/docs/$.tsx`      | `/docs/*`     |

## Path params [#path-params]

* `$param` → `:param`
* `$` → `*` (splat, at file level, e.g. `docs/$.tsx` → `/docs/*`)
* `index` → root of directory

## Matching [#matching]

`matchPath(pattern, pathname)` → `{id}` params or null. Wildcard matches multiple segments.

## Layouts [#layouts]

Root `src/ui/layouts/root.tsx`; nested layouts possible.

## Typed routes [#typed-routes]

`src/.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts` — regenerated by `kwiva build` and `kwiva dev`.


# RPC Client (/docs/frontend/rpc-client)



# RPC Client [#rpc-client]

`@kwiva/client` — scoped, typed client, SSR-safe.

## `client` singleton [#client-singleton]

```ts
import { client } from "@kwiva/client";
const todos = await client.Todos.list({ query: { page: 1 } });
```

## `useResource` — hooks for lists and singles [#useresource--hooks-for-lists-and-singles]

```tsx
const { data, isLoading } = useResource("TodosController.list", { query: { page: 1 } });
```

## Subscriptions [#subscriptions]

`connectRoute(routeId, args, {reconnect?, handlers?, onEvent?})` — WS.

## Testing [#testing]

With `withApp`, `ctx.client` is the in-process typed client.

> \[!TIP]
> TanStack Query in the background; `@tanstack/react-query` is a peer dep.


# UI Components (/docs/frontend/ui-components)



# UI Components [#ui-components]

Kwiva ships its own minimal UI kit built on Base UI + Tailwind v4.

## Theme (kwiva tokens) [#theme-kwiva-tokens]

From `src/app.css` — Kwiva design tokens (`--color-kwiva-*`), CSS utilities.

## Primitives [#primitives]

* **Pages/Layouts** — `definePage`, `layoutSegments`, `resolveLayouts`
* **Islands** — `defineIsland`, `renderIsland`
* **SSR** — `renderPage`, `streamPage`, `assetTags`, `hydrateApp`, `Link`, `setLinkPrefetcher`, `installScrollRestoration`
* **ErrorBoundary** — class, `fallback` + `onError`

## Utilities [#utilities]

`deterministicHash`, `useClickOutside`, `flattenMenu`, `dragStateResolver` (builder), `constrainDraggable`, `sanitizeStyleQuery`, `cn`, `extractSegmentClasses`, `mergeClassName`, `convertToDataTabs`, `toSectionNav` — internal.

## Rendering entry points [#rendering-entry-points]

From `@kwiva/ui/server` — `renderPage`, `discoverLayouts`, etc.

## Patterns [#patterns]

* **DataTable** — via `useResource` + Islands for interactivity
* **Forms** — `useForm` + Islands for validation
* **Modals** — via `PageRedirect`/`notFound` + Islands

> \[!TIP]
> UI is optional — apps can use any UI framework. Kwiva's built-in kit is minimal and typed.


# Configuration (/docs/getting-started/configuration)



# Configuration [#configuration]

Kwiva is typed-config-first: every behavior knob lives in `src/config/*.ts` as a section.

## Precedence [#precedence]

1. **Built-in defaults** (core): `app: {port: 3000, host: "localhost"}`, `logger: {level: "info", sink: "console"}`, `cache: {driver: "memory", prefix: "kwiva", defaultTtl: 60000, tags: true, swrGraceMs: 60000}`, `kv: {driver: "memory", namespace: "app", defaultTtl: 300000}`.
2. **Files** — `src/config/app.ts`, `database.ts`, `auth.ts`, `client.ts`, `jobs.ts`, `events.ts`, `mail.ts`, `storage.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `cache.ts`, `kv.ts`, `search.ts` — section name = filename.
3. **Environment overrides** — `SECTION_KEY` in upper-snake (`APP_PORT`, `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_POOL_MAX`, `AUTH_SESSION_SECRET`, `MCP_ROUTE`).

## File form [#file-form]

```ts title="src/config/database.ts"
import { defineConfig } from "@kwiva/core";

export default defineConfig({
  driver: "pglite",
  // or "postgres" + url/host/port/username/password/pool
});
```

Sections whose `validate*` runs in `applyConfigSections` (boot seam): `auth`, `jobs`, `client`, `events`, `storage`, `mail`, `mcp`, `search`. `database` → `configureDatabase`.

## Key sections table [#key-sections-table]

| Section    | Owner   | Shape                                                                             |
| ---------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `app`      | core    | `{name?, port?, host?}`                                                           |
| `logger`   | core    | `{level?, sink?}`                                                                 |
| `cache`    | core    | `{driver?, prefix?, defaultTtl?, tags?, swrGraceMs?}`                             |
| `kv`       | core    | `{driver?, namespace?, defaultTtl?}`                                              |
| `database` | data    | `DatabaseConfig{driver: "pglite"\|"postgres", url?, dataDir?, pool?}` + `tenancy` |
| `auth`     | auth    | `AuthConfig` (providers/session)                                                  |
| `client`   | client  | `ClientConfig{baseUrl, credentials?, fetch?, onError?}`                           |
| `jobs`     | jobs    | `JobsConfig{driver, defaultQueue?, concurrency?, scheduler?}`                     |
| `events`   | events  | `EventsConfig{driver?, prefix?}`                                                  |
| `mail`     | mail    | `MailConfig{transport?, from?}`                                                   |
| `storage`  | storage | `StorageConfig{default?, disks?, tenant?}`                                        |
| `mcp`      | mcp     | `McpConfig{enabled?, route?, transport?, auth?, models?, ...}`                    |
| `search`   | search  | `SearchConfig{engine: "postgres"}`                                                |

Environment variable names are derived by `envVarFor(section, keyPath)` — e.g. `client.baseUrl` → `CLIENT_BASE_URL`.

## Loading (from `@kwiva/core`) [#loading-from-kwivacore]

`loadConfig("src/config", root, env(), validators?)` → `Promise<ConfigDefinition>` (frozen). Validators run after merge; section `validateX` functions are invoked via `applyConfigSections`.


# Create a Project (/docs/getting-started/create-project)



# Create a Project [#create-a-project]

`kwiva create <name>` scaffolds a new app directory.

## Syntax [#syntax]

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva create my-app
```

Name validation: `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` (lowercase letters, digits, dashes; starts with a letter). Errors → stderr + exit 1.

## What gets scaffolded [#what-gets-scaffolded]

| Path                                                | Purpose                                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `bootstrap/app.ts`                                  | `defineApp({name})` entry              |
| `src/config/app.ts`                                 | `{port: 3000}`                         |
| `src/config/database.ts`                            | `driver: "pglite"` (in-memory default) |
| `src/config/cache.ts`, `src/config/kv.ts`           | `driver: "memory"`                     |
| `src/config/storage.ts`                             | tenant scoping enabled                 |
| `src/config/mcp.ts`                                 | `enabled: false`                       |
| `src/app/models/`                                   | empty models folder                    |
| `src/app/http/controllers/`                         | —                                      |
| `src/database/migrations/`, `src/database/seeders/` | —                                      |
| `package.json`                                      | scripts: `dev`, `build`, `test`        |

Logs `kwiva create → scaffolded <target>`.

## Next steps [#next-steps]

```bash title="terminal"
cd my-app
bun install
kwiva dev
```

`kwiva dev` serves on port 3000 with hot reload (client-only changes don't respawn the server).


# Development Server (/docs/getting-started/development-server)



# Development Server [#development-server]

`kwiva dev` builds the client bundle, writes `src/.kwiva/serve.gen.ts` (a stub server booting the app), and spawns a child process.

## Syntax [#syntax]

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva dev --port 4000
```

* `--port` default: `3000`. Invalid (non-integer or \< 1) → stderr + exit 1.
* Rebuilds client bundle on changes (client-only changes, excluding `src/.kwiva/`, rebuild without respawn).
* Full app changes spawn a new server process.
* `src/.kwiva/dist/<app>` — bumpGeneration on serve.
* Exit on SIGINT/SIGTERM → exit 0 (supervisor.stop()).

## Reload notification (SSE) [#reload-notification-sse]

The dev server emits `src/.kwiva/dist/<app>/src/app/jobs/*.ts`, `src/app/events/*.ts`, `src/app/commands/*.ts` — you can't define modules you don't import.

## Bootstrap notes [#bootstrap-notes]

* App is booted with `bun src/.kwiva/serve.gen.ts <root> <port>`.
* `kwiva dev` runs until interrupted.

> \[!TIP]
> For the app, `bootstrap/app.ts` is the entry: `export default defineApp({name})` + `await configureApp()`.


# Your First API (/docs/getting-started/first-api)



# Your First API [#your-first-api]

## The Free API from your model [#the-free-api-from-your-model]

Every `defineModel` gets 5 generated routes (REST per model):

```plaintext title="free-api.txt"
GET    /api/todos
POST   /api/todos
GET    /api/todos/:id
PATCH  /api/todos/:id
DELETE /api/todos/:id
```

## Controllers [#controllers]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/todos.ts"
import { defineController } from "@kwiva/http";
import { requireAuth } from "@kwiva/auth";
import { authorize } from "@kwiva/auth";

export const TodosController = defineController({
  prefix: "/api/todos",
  permission: "todos",
  middleware: [requireAuth()],
  routes(api) {
    api.get("/", async (ctx) => {
      return ctx.store.todos.where("status", "pending").all();
    });

    api.post("/", (ctx) => {
      authorize(TodoPolicy, ctx.user, "create");
      return ctx.store.todos.create(ctx.input.body).toJSON();
    }, { name: "create" });
  },
});
```

## A complete controller with contracts [#a-complete-controller-with-contracts]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/posts.ts"
import { defineController } from "@kwiva/http";
import { validateTodoInput } from "../validators";

export const PostsController = defineController({
  prefix: "/api/todos",
  routes(api) {
    api.get("/", () => ({ items: [] }));
    api.get("/:id", () => ({ id: 1 }));
    api.post("/", (ctx) => ctx.input.body, {
      name: "create",
      input: { body: CreateTodoBody },
      output: { schema: TodoJson, status: 201 },
    });
  },
});
```

## How it wires [#how-it-wires]

```plaintext
GET /api/todos/
├── parser.parse() → ctx.input
├── input.validate() (Standard Schema) → 400 VALIDATION on failure
├── middleware → 401/403
├── handler → result
└── output.transform() → json
```

## What to read next [#what-to-read-next]

* [REST conventions](/docs/api/rest)
* [Generated endpoints](/docs/api/generated-endpoints)
* [Typed RPC](/docs/api/rpc)
* [Client SDK](/docs/api/client)


# Your First Deployment (/docs/getting-started/first-deployment)



# Your First Deployment [#your-first-deployment]

```bash title="terminal"
bun install
kwiva dev --port 4000
kwiva build
```

## Build output [#build-output]

`kwiva build`:

1. Regenerates route tree (`src/.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts`) + client bundle (`src/.kwiva/entry.client.tsx`).
2. Writes `<out>/client` — default out dir is `dist` (there's no separate prod-bundle flag needed).

## Runtime modes [#runtime-modes]

| Mode          | Target                                                                                                             | Notes |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----- |
| Bun (default) | `bun src/index.ts` — actually `bun src/.kwiva/serve.gen.ts` per dev — production: `bun dist/`...                   | —     |
| Node          | `bun build --target=node` via `--preset=node`? — kwiva build has no preset; use `.output/server/index.mjs`? — skip |       |
| Serverless    | API-only output — adapters                                                                                         | —     |

> \[!TIP]
> Kwiva's main supported deploy targets: standalone servers (Bun/Node), serverless (API-only), containers (Docker). Edge presets exist in principle but apps route to presets per target (`--target`).

## Production checklist [#production-checklist]

```plaintext
[ ] bun install — lockfile
[ ] kwiva migrate — apply pending migrations
[ ] kwiva seed — seed data
[ ] APP_KEY set — `kwiva key:generate`
[ ] MCP_ROUTE on (only if needed)
```

## What to read next [#what-to-read-next]

* [Runtime Adapters](/docs/deployment/adapters)
* [Node/Bun Deployment](/docs/deployment/node-bun)
* [Serverless](/docs/deployment/serverless)
* [Containers](/docs/deployment/containers)
* [Production Checklist](/docs/deployment/production-checklist)


# Your First Model (/docs/getting-started/first-model)



# Your First Model [#your-first-model]

```ts title="src/app/models/todo.ts"
import { defineModel } from "@kwiva/data";

export const Todo = defineModel("todos", (f) => ({
  id: f.id(),
  title: f.string().validation((s) => s.min(1).max(200)),
  status: f.enum("pending", "done"),
  priority: f.integer().default(0),
  createdAt: f.dateTime(),
  updatedAt: f.dateTime(),
}), {
  timestamps: true,
  routes: true,
  fillable: ["title", "status", "priority"],
  permission: "todos",
});
```

## What this model derives [#what-this-model-derives]

| Artifact       | Description                                                                                                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Database table | From field kinds — `string` → `varchar`, `integer` → `integer`, etc.                                       |
| Migrations     | SQL-step `defineMigration` files in `src/database/migrations/`                                             |
| REST routes    | `GET /api/todos`, `GET /api/todos/:id`, `POST /api/todos`, `PATCH /api/todos/:id`, `DELETE /api/todos/:id` |
| Typed client   | `client.Todos.list()`, `client.Todos.get(1)`, …                                                            |
| MCP tools      | `todos_list`, `todos_create`, … (when `mcp.models` opts in)                                                |
| OpenAPI        | Model schema in `/openapi.json`                                                                            |

## Field DSL [#field-dsl]

| Method                                                              | Type             | Notes                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `f.id()`                                                            | `integer, pk`    | —                                                                |
| `f.uuid()`                                                          | `uuid, pk`       | —                                                                |
| `f.string()`                                                        | `varchar`        | `.nullable(), .indexed(), .unique(), .validation(v => v.min(1))` |
| `f.text()`, `f.integer()`, `f.bigint()`, `f.float()`, `f.boolean()` | —                | —                                                                |
| `f.dateTime()`                                                      | `timestamp`      | —                                                                |
| `f.enum(...values)`                                                 | check constraint | —                                                                |
| `f.json<T>()`                                                       | json             | —                                                                |
| `f.belongsTo(() => Model)`                                          | FK column        | `nullable(), optional()`                                         |
| `f.hasMany(() => Model)`                                            | —                | reverse of belongsTo                                             |

## Verify + migrate [#verify--migrate]

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva migrate
kwiva route:list
bun run test
```

> \[!TIP]
> In development, Kwiva auto-runs migrations on boot when in dev mode (`kwiva dev`).


# Your First Page (/docs/getting-started/first-page)



# Your First Page [#your-first-page]

```tsx title="src/ui/pages/index.tsx"
import { definePage } from "@kwiva/ui";

export default definePage({
  load(ctx) {
    const todos = await ctx.store.todos.all();
    return { todos };
  },
  render({ props }) {
    return <main><ul>{props.todos.map((t) => <li>{t.title}</li>)}</ul></main>;
  },
  head() {
    return { title: "My App — Todos" };
  },
});
```

## definePage contract [#definepage-contract]

| Field           | Type                           | Notes                                                  |
| --------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `load(ctx)`     | `(ctx: HttpContext) => object` | server-side, SSR-only data                             |
| `render(props)` | `ReactElement`                 | —                                                      |
| `head()`        | `PageHead`                     | `{title?, meta?, link?, canonical?, jsonLd?, robots?}` |
| `middleware`    | `Middleware[]`                 | —                                                      |
| `path`          | string                         | when using `definePage(path, options)` form            |

## Routing [#routing]

`src/ui/pages/**` files map to routes:

| File                           | Route        |
| ------------------------------ | ------------ |
| `src/ui/pages/index.tsx`       | `/`          |
| `src/ui/pages/todos.$id.tsx`   | `/todos/:id` |
| `src/ui/pages/todos/index.tsx` | `/todos`     |

`$param` → `:param`, `$` → `*` (splat). Layouts in `src/ui/layouts/` wrap pages (`root.tsx` is the root layout).

## How SSR works [#how-ssr-works]

```plaintext
GET /todos/$id
├── resolveRoute(pathname) → page module
├── page.load(ctx) → props (server, streaming)
├── layout.render(props, ctx)
└── document → Response
```

## What to read next [#what-to-read-next]

* [UI Components](/docs/frontend/ui-components)
* [Routing](/docs/frontend/routing)
* [Data Hooks](/docs/frontend/data-hooks)
* [Streaming SSR](/docs/rendering/streaming)


# Installation (/docs/getting-started)



Getting a Kwiva application running is a two-step process: install the runtime, then scaffold a project. Kwiva runs on [Bun](https://bun.sh) as its primary runtime, which executes TypeScript natively — no compile step, fast startup, and a single runtime for both your server and your tools.

## Prerequisites [#prerequisites]

| Requirement | Version        | Notes                                                              |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Bun**     | 1.2 or later   | Primary runtime — required for the CLI, the dev server, and builds |
| **Node.js** | 18+ (optional) | For `node_server` compatibility presets and legacy integrations    |
| **Git**     | any (optional) | For version control and addon installs from git                    |

Install or upgrade Bun:

```bash title="terminal"
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
bun --version
```

> \[!NOTE]
> Kwiva is *not* a library layered on top of an existing app. The scaffold creates a complete project with its own configuration, directory conventions, and CLI — you don't wire pieces together afterwards.

## Create a Project [#create-a-project]

The fastest way to start a Kwiva project is a single scaffold command:

<Tabs items="['Bun (recommended)', 'Direct CLI']">
  <Tab value="Bun (recommended)">
    ```bash
    bun create kwiva my-app
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab value="Direct CLI">
    ```bash
    bunx kwiva new my-app
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

This is equivalent to `kwiva new my-app`. It creates a new project in `my-app/` with the default **fullstack** mode — a complete application with SSR frontend pages, API routes, and everything configured with sensible defaults. The scaffold installs dependencies, generates `kwiva.config.ts`, and prepares empty directories for models, controllers, and pages.

### Project Modes [#project-modes]

Choose a mode that matches how your application will run. The mode is set once at scaffold time and stays baked into the project's defaults.

```bash title="terminal"
# Specify a mode
bun create kwiva my-app --mode=api+spa
```

| Mode         | Description                                   | Deploy default                     |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `fullstack`  | SSR pages + API routes (default)              | `node_server`, auto-detected in CI |
| `api+spa`    | API server + single-page app frontend         | `node_server` + client build       |
| `static`     | Static site generation — prerender everything | `static`                           |
| `standalone` | API-only, single-file binary output           | `bun-server` + compiled binary     |
| `edge`       | Optimized for edge runtimes                   | `cloudflare_worker`                |

Each mode is a trimmed profile of the same framework; switching to a richer mode later is a matter of adding the directories the mode omits. See [Create a Project](/docs/getting-started/create-project) for a full comparison.

## What You Can Build [#what-you-can-build]

The same conventions carry you from a static site to a high-scale platform. A useful roster of examples:

| From                  | To                                                      | What you add                                               |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Static marketing site | [Static site + blog](/docs/getting-started/first-model) | A read-only model, file-based pages, prerendering          |
| CRUD app              | Classic todo-style app                                  | One `defineModel` derives the REST API, client, and Studio |
| SaaS                  | Dashboard with auth + RBAC                              | `defineAuth`, policies, guards, Studio screens             |
| Realtime              | Multi-tenant chat                                       | Tenancy config, events, channels, jobs                     |
| API-only              | Backend for a mobile client                             | Controllers, OpenAPI, rate limits, API keys                |
| AI ops                | Internal tool with MCP exposure                         | Kwiva Studio over models, MCP tools                        |
| Platform              | Edge + ISR + worker split                               | Route rules, transactional outbox, deploy presets          |

Whatever the shape, the stack is the same: models as the single source of truth, controllers for the API, pages for the UI, and one config model connecting them.

## A First Tour of the CLI [#a-first-tour-of-the-cli]

Everything you do with a Kwiva project goes through one `kwiva` binary (run through `bun run` in your project):

| Command             | Purpose                                              |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `kwiva dev`         | Development server with hot module replacement       |
| `kwiva check`       | Format + lint + typecheck in one pass                |
| `kwiva test`        | Run the test suite (unit, integration, API, and e2e) |
| `kwiva build`       | Production build for the target runtime              |
| `kwiva deploy`      | Build and deploy to a provider                       |
| `kwiva console`     | REPL with the full app context loaded                |
| `kwiva make:*`      | Generators — one command per construct type          |
| `kwiva db:*`        | Database lifecycle — migrations, seeding, reset      |
| `kwiva add <addon>` | Install and register a module, plugin, or theme      |
| `kwiva upgrade`     | Codemod recipes + dependency bumps across releases   |

You'll use `kwiva make:model`, `kwiva db:migrate`, and `kwiva dev` heavily in the tutorials that follow. The CLI is described in full at [CLI](/docs/cli).

## Start the Development Server [#start-the-development-server]

```bash title="terminal"
cd my-app
bun run dev
```

The development server starts at `http://localhost:3000` and gives you:

* **Native TypeScript execution** — Bun runs `.ts` files directly, no compile step between edit and reload
* **Hot module replacement (HMR)** — pages, controllers, and middleware update in place
* **Auto-discovery** — models, controllers, middleware, and pages in the conventional directories are picked up automatically
* **Typed configuration** — your config folder and environment variables load and validate at boot
* **Friendly errors** — missing environment variables, type errors, and runtime failures are surfaced with context instead of raw stack dumps

> \[!TIP]
> Open `http://localhost:3000` right after scaffolding — the default fullstack project ships with a working home page backed by the whole pipeline. See [Development Server](/docs/getting-started/development-server) for what happens under the hood.

## The First Five Minutes [#the-first-five-minutes]

A fast first loop that exercises the whole stack:

```bash title="terminal"
bun create kwiva my-app && cd my-app
bun run dev                     # home page at localhost:3000
kwiva make:model post           # model + migration + factory stub
kwiva db:migrate                # apply it
kwiva make:page posts.$id       # a typed page stub
```

From here you have a data model serving a page — with types flowing from model to database to API to UI. The rest of this guide deepens each step.

## FAQ [#faq]

<Accordions type="single">
  <Accordion title="Is Kwiva a library I add to an existing app?">
    No. The scaffold creates a complete project with its own configuration, directory conventions, and CLI. You build on the framework, not alongside it — there is no wiring step afterwards.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Which runtimes does Kwiva support?">
    Bun is the primary runtime. Node-compatible output is available through deployment presets, and the `edge` mode targets edge runtimes with a documented constraint set. Deploying to a target is a build-time choice.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Which project mode should I choose?">
    Start with the default `fullstack` mode. Choose `static` for a marketing site, `api+spa` when you want a separate client, `standalone` for a single binary, or `edge` for edge runtimes. Modes are trimmed profiles of the same layout — you can add the omitted directories later.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What does the scaffold actually include?">
    A working home page, `kwiva.config.ts`, the typed config folder, and conventional directories for models, controllers, middleware, pages, jobs, and events — plus the CLI wired up. The first model you define is served by a full pipeline, not a stub.
  </Accordion>
</Accordions>

## What's Next [#whats-next]

After installation, follow the getting-started sequence to build your first real feature:

1. [Understand the project structure](/docs/getting-started/project-structure) — where every kind of file lives
2. [Configure your application](/docs/getting-started/configuration) — typed config modules and env bindings
3. [Create your first model](/docs/getting-started/first-model) — the single source of truth for your data
4. [Create your first API](/docs/getting-started/first-api) — controllers, validation, and typed context
5. [Create your first page](/docs/getting-started/first-page) — server-rendered UI with typed loaders
6. [Deploy your first app](/docs/getting-started/first-deployment) — build once, deploy anywhere


# Project Structure (/docs/getting-started/project-structure)



# Project Structure [#project-structure]

```
my-app/
├── bootstrap/
│   └── app.ts                  # defineApp({ name })
├── src/
│   ├── config/                 # app, database, cache, kv, storage, mcp, ...
│   ├── app/                    # discoverable app constructs
│   │   ├── models/             # src/app/models/*.ts
│   │   ├── controllers/...     # src/app/http/controllers/*.ts
│   │   ├── middleware/...      # src/app/http/middleware/*.ts
│   │   ├── policies/           # src/app/policies/*.ts (Policy + Gate)
│   │   ├── services/           # src/app/services/*.ts
│   │   ├── jobs/               # src/app/jobs/*.ts
│   │   ├── tasks/              # src/app/tasks/*.ts
│   │   ├── events/             # src/app/events/*.ts (Event + Listener + Subscriber)
│   │   └── commands/           # src/app/commands/*.ts (defineCommand)
│   ├── ui/
│   │   ├── pages/              # definePage files (*.tsx)
│   │   └── layouts/            # layouts/*.tsx
│   └── database/
│       ├── migrations/         # timestamped SQL-step migrations
│       └── seeders/            # idempotent seeders
└── .kwiva/                     # generated: route-tree.gen.ts, serve.gen.ts, entry.client.tsx
```

## Key rules [#key-rules]

* `src/app/**` and `src/ui/**` are convention folders — everything inside is discovered by name.
* Files exporting `defineX` factories are auto-discovered by convention (see [Auto-Discovery](/docs/core-concepts/auto-discovery)).
* One construct per file, in its own directory: models → `src/app/models/`, pages → `src/ui/pages/`, etc.
* Config files: `src/config/*.ts` — one file per section (section key = filename).
* `src/.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts` is the **typed route map** consumed by `@kwiva/client`, `@kwiva/ui`, and editors (regenerated by `kwiva build` and `kwiva dev`).


# Response Caching (/docs/http/caching)



# Response Caching [#response-caching]

## Route caching [#route-caching]

`ctx.response.set({cache: {ttl, swr}})` on handler → cytokine.

## Model caching (future) [#model-caching-future]

Model-level caching via `ctx.bound.store` (evlog-style?) — see advanced.

## Client caching [#client-caching]

TanStack Query cache in `@kwiva/client` — see [Data Hooks](/docs/frontend/data-hooks).

> \[!TIP]
> For full cache implementation docs, see [Cache & KV](/docs/data/cache) + [Cache & KV (core)](/api/core#cache-advisory).


# Controllers (/docs/http/controllers)



# Controllers [#controllers]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/posts.ts"
import { defineController } from "@kwiva/http";

export const PostsController = defineController({
  prefix: "/api/posts",
  permission: "posts",
  routes(api) {
    api.get("/", (ctx) => ctx.store.posts.where("status", "pending").all());
    api.get("/:id", (ctx) => ctx.store.posts.find(ctx.params.id));
    api.post("/", (ctx) => ctx.store.posts.create(ctx.input.body), {
      name: "create",
      input: { body: CreatePostContract },
    });
  },
});
```

## Route builder methods [#route-builder-methods]

| Method                                                                   | Purpose                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------- |
| `api.get(path, handler, options?)` / `post` / `put` / `patch` / `delete` | handler + options                 |
| `api.ws(path, { input?, handler(ctx): AsyncGenerator }, macros?)`        | WebSocket route                   |
| `api.guard(scope, setup?)`                                               | guard middleware scope            |
| `api.group(options, setup?)`                                             | scoped middleware + route builder |

### Route options (2nd arg) [#route-options-2nd-arg]

| Option                                                    | Type                                          | Notes                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `input`                                                   | `{params?, query?, body?, headers?, cookie?}` | sections with Standard Schema                         |
| `output`                                                  | `{schema?, status?, transform?}`              | response contract                                     |
| `contract`                                                | `Contract`                                    | merged contract (`defineContract`)                    |
| `middleware`                                              | `Middleware[]`                                | route-level                                           |
| `bind`                                                    | `{from, as, list?}`                           | resolvers (see [Middleware](/docs/http/middleware))   |
| `handler`                                                 | `fn`                                          | —                                                     |
| `name`                                                    | string                                        | unique route id suffix                                |
| `namePrefix`                                              | string                                        | —                                                     |
| `tags`, `summary`, `description`, `openAPI`, `deprecated` | —                                             | OpenAPI metadata                                      |
| `permission`                                              | string                                        | policy namespace for the route (overrides controller) |
| `beforeHandle`, `afterHandle`                             | `Middleware[]`                                | —                                                     |
| `macros`                                                  | `Record<string, MacroDefinition>`             | —                                                     |

## Controller options [#controller-options]

| Option             | Notes                            |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| `prefix`           | route path prefix (`/api/posts`) |
| `middleware`       | controller-level middleware      |
| `middlewareGroups` | named refs to global middleware  |
| `routes(api)`      | builder callback                 |
| `tags`             | OpenAPI tags                     |

## Typed context — `ctx` [#typed-context--ctx]

| Member                                                  | Notes                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `ctx.input`                                             | destructured `{params, query, body, headers, cookies}` |
| `ctx.params` / `ctx.query` / `ctx.body`                 | raw sections                                           |
| `ctx.headers()` / `ctx.setHeaders()`                    | response headers                                       |
| `ctx.json()` / `ctx.text()` / `ctx.noContent()`         | response                                               |
| `ctx.redirect(url, status?)` / `ctx.away(url, status?)` | ambient helpers                                        |
| `ctx.waitUntil(promise)`                                | —                                                      |
| `ctx.session` / `ctx.user` / `ctx.can`                  | auth context                                           |
| `ctx.bound(key)`                                        | resolver result                                        |

## Mounting [#mounting]

`bootApp(server, {controllers, middlewareGroups, models, macros, resolvers, appCtx, openAPI})` → `bindRouteIds` per controller → routes + manifest + OpenAPI mount. `findRoute(entries, name)`, `routeUrl(entries, name, params?)`.

> \[!TIP]
> 404s for unknown routes use the 404 handler in `ctx.error`; controller returns; nothing throws.


# CORS & Security Headers (/docs/http/cors)



# CORS & Security Headers [#cors--security-headers]

## `cors` middleware [#cors-middleware]

```ts title="src/app/http/middleware/cors.ts"
import { cors, defineMiddleware } from "@kwiva/http";
export const GlobalCors = defineMiddleware((ctx, next) => {
  return cors({ origin: "https://example.com", credentials: true })(ctx, next);
});
```

## `csrf` middleware [#csrf-middleware]

Double-submit / cookie HMAC check; `exempt` for auth-exempt routes.

## `rateLimit` middleware [#ratelimit-middleware]

Throws `RATE_LIMITED` (429) on exceed; `key` configurable; `resetRateLimits()` to clear.

## Default security headers [#default-security-headers]

`x-content-type-options: nosniff`, `x-frame-options: DENY`, `strict-transport-security`, `cross-origin-resource-policy: same-origin`, `referrer-policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `permissions-policy` (restricted), `x-goog-results`, no-store for non-CDN.

## CSP [#csp]

See [Security → Headers](/docs/security/headers).

> \[!TIP]
> For local dev, set `x-content-type-options: nosniff` off — dev-only setting via `secure`/`env`.


# Errors (/docs/http/errors)



# Errors [#errors]

## Error taxonomy (`@kwiva/core`) [#error-taxonomy-kwivacore]

| Code           | HTTP | Throwable class                   |
| -------------- | ---- | --------------------------------- |
| `BAD_REQUEST`  | 400  | `BadRequestError` (implicit base) |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401  | `UnauthorizedError`               |
| `FORBIDDEN`    | 403  | `ForbiddenError`                  |
| `NOT_FOUND`    | 404  | `NotFoundError`                   |
| `CONFLICT`     | 409  | `ConflictError`                   |
| `VALIDATION`   | 422  | `ValidationError` (+ `fields`)    |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429  | `RateLimitedError`                |
| `INTERNAL`     | 500  | default                           |

Plus storage/search: `STORAGE_NOT_FOUND/CONFLICT/INVALID/UNAVAILABLE/TENANT_REQUIRED`, `SEARCH_NOT_CONFIGURED`.

## Throwing errors [#throwing-errors]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/posts.ts"
api.get("/:id", async (ctx) => {
  const post = await Post.findOrFail(ctx.params.id);
});
```

`error(code, message, data?)` — from `@kwiva/core`.

## Error handlers [#error-handlers]

```ts
ctx.error(code, message, fields?); // return error
```

## Error response shape [#error-response-shape]

```json title="Validation"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION",
    "message": "Invalid input",
    "fields": { "body.title": ["Too short"] },
    "requestId": "req_abc123"
  }
}
```

## Validation issues → field map [#validation-issues--field-map]

`issuesToFields(issues)` — `Record<string, string[]>`.

## Custom error codes [#custom-error-codes]

Extend `ErrorCode` with `KwivaErrorOptions` — throw `error("CUSTOM", "msg")` in handler.
