## Client-side [#client-side]

`@kwiva/client`: `toClientError(status, value)` → `ClientErrorShape{code, message, status, fields?, requestId?}`; `onError` config hook; typed discriminant by code.


# File Uploads (/docs/http/file-uploads)



# File Uploads [#file-uploads]

## `ctx.file()` [#ctxfile]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/avatars.ts"
api.post("/", async (ctx) => {
  const [file] = ctx.file("avatar"); // Array<UploadedFile>
  if (!file) throw new Error("missing file");
  const { key } = await storage.put(file.name, await file.arrayBuffer(), { contentType: file.type });
  return { key, url: storage.disk().url(key) };
});
```

`UploadedFile` — has `name`, `type`, `size`, `arrayBuffer()`, `text()`, `stream()`, `blob()`.

## Validation [#validation]

* `ctx.file()` throws if missing (NOT\_FOUND/BAD\_REQUEST).
* Field-level: `contentType` regex, `size` max — via input contract.

## `storage` integration [#storage-integration]

See [File Storage](/docs/data/storage).

## `@kwiva/client` uploads [#kwivaclient-uploads]

`useUpload(routeId)` — multipart via FormData, or direct object from `client.Files.put(...)`.

## Example — `storage:put` endpoint [#example--storageput-endpoint]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/storage-files.ts"
export const StorageFilesController = defineController({
  prefix: "/api/files",
  routes(api) {
    api.post("/", async (ctx) => {
      const [file] = ctx.file("file");
      const put = await storage.signedUploadUrl(file.name, { expiresIn: 60_000, maxSize: 10_000_000 });
      return put;
    }, { name: "upload-url", input: { file: FileContract } });
  },
});
```

> \[!TIP]
> For large files, use presigned URLs directly from the browser/CLI.


# Guards (/docs/http/guards)



# Guards [#guards]

Guards are middleware-typed authorization checks — defined inline or named, applied at route level.

## `api.guard(scope, setup)` [#apiguardscope-setup]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/admin.ts"
export const AdminController = defineController({
  prefix: "/api/admin",
  routes(api) {
    api.guard(
      { name: "is-admin", beforeHandle: async () => {
          if (!ctx.user?.role === "admin") throw new ForbiddenError("Admins only");
        } },
      (api) => {
        api.get("/stats", async () => ({ ok: true }));
      },
    );
  },
});
```

## Standalone `guard(builder, options, setup)` [#standalone-guardbuilder-options-setup]

```ts
import { guard, defineMiddleware } from "@kwiva/http";
const RequireRights = guard(defineMiddleware((ctx, next) => next(ctx)), {
  name: "posts-reader",
  allow: ["posts.read"],
}, (api) => api.get("/posts", async () => ({ items: [] })));
```

## Guard options [#guard-options]

| Option         | Notes                          |
| -------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `name`         | guard scope name               |
| `beforeHandle` | middleware runs before handler |
| `middleware`   | additional middleware          |
| `bind`         | resolvers                      |
| `nest`         | deeper scoping                 |

## Nesting/composition [#nestingcomposition]

* Guards compose: outer + inner run in order.
* `api.guard` can be used inside `api.group`.

## Access via `ctx` [#access-via-ctx]

* `ctx.user.id`, `ctx.can`, `ctx.authorize(...)`? — `can(policy, user, action, resource?)` from `@kwiva/auth`; `ctx.can` ambient.
* `ctx.permission` — controller-level permission string.

## Guard policies are per-route [#guard-policies-are-per-route]

`api.post("/", handler, { permission: "posts.create" })` → framework checks `ctx.can("posts.create")` if configured.

> \[!TIP]
> Guards with `policy: "name"` reference `src/app/policies/<name>.ts` — see [Policies](/docs/authorization/policies).


# HTTP (/docs/http)



# HTTP [#http]

Framework-owned HTTP layer: controllers, contracts, middleware, routing, validation, errors, caching.

## Layer diagram [#layer-diagram]

```
Elysia (HTTP server, sealed)
├── Pipeline (parse → validate → middleware → handler → output)
├── Controllers (defineController) → auto-manifest → dev-overlay wiring
├── WebSocket routes + channels
├── REST auto-routes (from @kwiva/data models)
└── OpenAPI (mountOpenAPI, Scalar at /docs)
```

## Entry points [#entry-points]

| Topic                          | Page                                       |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| Controllers (defineController) | [Controllers](/docs/http/controllers)      |
| Routes & routing               | [Routes & Routing](/docs/http/routes)      |
| Middleware                     | [Middleware](/docs/http/middleware)        |
| Request lifecycle              | [Request Lifecycle](/docs/http/lifecycle)  |
| Guards                         | [Guards](/docs/http/guards)                |
| Validation                     | [Validation](/docs/http/validation)        |
| Error handling (8 codes)       | [Errors](/docs/http/errors)                |
| File uploads                   | [File Uploads](/docs/http/file-uploads)    |
| Streaming & SSE                | [Streaming & SSE](/docs/http/streaming)    |
| WebSockets                     | [WebSockets](/docs/http/websockets)        |
| CORS & Security Headers        | [CORS & Security Headers](/docs/http/cors) |
| Response Caching (route rules) | [Response Caching](/docs/http/caching)     |

## Key concepts [#key-concepts]

* **`defineController(name, routes, options)`** — one controller = prefix + routes + middleware + tags.
* **Auto-manifest** — `mountRoutes` binds route IDs (`ControllerName.verb`).
* **`ctx`** — `HttpContext`: `input{params, query, body, headers, cookies}`, `setHeaders()`, `json()`, `text()`, `redirect()`, `stream()`, `session`, `user`, `can`.
* **REST auto-routes** — `@kwiva/data` `restRoutes`: `GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/{plural}` + `/:id` + `:id/actions` (5 per model).
* **OpenAPI** — `mountOpenAPI(app, manifest)` + `/docs` (Scalar) + `/openapi.json`.


# Request Lifecycle (/docs/http/lifecycle)



# Request Lifecycle [#request-lifecycle]

## Standard pipeline [#standard-pipeline]

```
1. Elysia → WebHandler
2. buildCtx — parse input (params/query/body/headers/cookies)
3. validateInput — per-route sections via Standard Schema → VALIDATION (422) on failure
4. compileBeforeHandle — run middleware stack (global → group → controller → route)
5. wrapHandler — handler via `ctx.input`, produce result
6. validateOutput — response schema via contract
7. toErrorResponse — error mapping (STORAGE_* → storage 404s; SEARCH_NOT_CONFIGURED → search 404)
8. Response returned (or afterHandle + waitUntil)
```

## Pipeline details (for advanced users) [#pipeline-details-for-advanced-users]

```ts
const body = resolveBody(part.value, route, overrides);
const partResult = splitInput(input); // {params, query, body, headers, cookies}
validateInput → {params, query, body, headers?, cookies?}

runMiddleware(steps, ctx); // preflight + controller + route
handler → result
validateOutput → value
```

## Error mapping [#error-mapping]

`toErrorResponse(error, requestId?)`:

| KwivaError code    | HTTP |
| ------------------ | ---- |
| BAD\_REQUEST       | 400  |
| UNAUTHORIZED       | 401  |
| FORBIDDEN          | 403  |
| NOT\_FOUND         | 404  |
| CONFLICT           | 409  |
| VALIDATION         | 422  |
| RATE\_LIMITED      | 429  |
| INTERNAL (default) | 500  |

`ctx.requestId` added to errors.

## WebSocket lifecycle [#websocket-lifecycle]

```
Elysia ws upgrade → policy check (channels) → subscribe
```

## Special cases [#special-cases]

* `ctx.waitUntil()` — after-response tasks (see [@kwiva/core async](/api/core#asyncclass-asyncmiddleware-afterresponse-onresponse-tasks-handler-types))
* Streaming: `ctx.stream()`, `stream(setup, {heartbeatMs, event})` — SSE.
* `Content-Type` handling for multipart (file uploads).

> \[!TIP]
> Custom error → use `ctx.error(code, msg, data)` in handler — appears in `errorResponse`.


# Middleware (/docs/http/middleware)



# Middleware [#middleware]

```ts title="src/app/http/middleware/logger.ts"
import { defineMiddleware } from "@kwiva/http";

export const Logger = defineMiddleware((ctx, next) => {
  const start = performance.now();
  try {
    return await next(ctx);
  } finally {
    ctx.logger.info("request.done", { ms: performance.now() - start });
  }
});
```

## Middleware lifecycle [#middleware-lifecycle]

```
Global → Group → Route (stack order) → handler
```

## MiddlewareStep [#middlewarestep]

```ts
type MiddlewareStep = (ctx: HttpContext, next: MiddlewareNext) => unknown;
```

* `await next(ctx)` — run downstream (may return response, or throw).
* Short-circuit: return `Response` (or `undefined` = pass through).
* `CONTINUE` symbol — with for-middleware helpers.

## Resolver binding [#resolver-binding]

```ts
export const BindPosts = defineMiddleware((ctx, next) => {
  ctx.bound.store = await resolvePosts(ctx);
  return next(ctx);
});
```

Resolvers: `resolveMiddlewareRefs(refs, groups)`, `resolveBindings(route, ctx)` — used in pipeline (`buildCtx`, `wrapHandler`).

## Scoping [#scoping]

| Scope      | Applied via                                      | Notes                 |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| Global     | `AppServer.mountPlugin(mw)` / `middlewareGroups` | —                     |
| Controller | `controller.middleware`                          | applies to all routes |
| Group      | `api.group({ middleware: [...] })`               | scoped sub-stacks     |
| Route      | `route.middleware`                               | per route             |

## Conditional/short-circuit [#conditionalshort-circuit]

* `ctx.request.method === "GET"` checks; return early without `await next()`.

## Built-in middleware [#built-in-middleware]

| Name                  | Purpose         | Notes                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cors(options?)`      | CORS            | `CorsOptions{origin, methods, headers, expose, credentials, maxAge}` — preflight support |
| `csrf(options?)`      | CSRF protection | `CsrfOptions{cookie, header, field, exempt, sameSite}` — double-submit or HMAC cookie    |
| `rateLimit(options?)` | Throttle        | `RateLimitOptions{max, windowMs, key, message}` — throws `RATE_LIMITED` (429)            |

`resetRateLimits()` clears internal state.

## Testing middleware [#testing-middleware]

`ctx.logger.info(...)`, `ctx.bound(key)` — middleware is testable via `withApp().handler(new Request("/"))` or `createTestClient`.

## Full reference [#full-reference]

`Middleware` type: `{step, preflight?}`; `resolveMiddleware(registry, ref)`; `MiddlewareGroupOptions{name, middleware[]}`.


# Routes & Routing (/docs/http/routes)



# Routes & Routing [#routes--routing]

* **Manifest**: `bootApp` → `ManifestEntry[]` (all routes from controllers).
* **Path params**: `:id` segments. Route resolution: `findRoute(entries, name)`.
* **Versioning**: `MCP v2; REST GET /api/:model` + `routeUrl(entries, "PostsController.list", { id })` — typed URLs.
* **Auto-routes**: `mountAutoRoutes` — `restRoutes` from models.
* **`defineRoute(options)`** — standalone routes for app code (non-controller).

## Five generated routes per model (REST) [#five-generated-routes-per-model-rest]

| Method          | Path               | Purpose                                  |
| --------------- | ------------------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| `GET`           | `/api/{model}`     | list (validated where/page/orderBy/with) |
| `POST`          | `/api/{model}`     | create (validated)                       |
| `GET`           | `/api/{model}/:id` | get                                      |
| `PATCH` / `PUT` | `/api/{model}/:id` | update                                   |
| `DELETE`        | `/api/{model}/:id` | remove                                   |

## Route naming [#route-naming]

* Controllers: `RouteId = "ControllerName.verb"` — verbs: `get→list`, `post→add/create`, `patch/put→update`, `delete→remove`, root `index→get`, param `:id→get`.
* `deriveRouteId(name, method, path)`.

## Middleware (named refs) [#middleware-named-refs]

Middleware can be registered as strings in `middleware: ["name"]` — `resolveMiddlewareRefs` maps names to Middleware (groups via `middlewareGroups`).

## 404 + method-not-allowed [#404--method-not-allowed]

* Unknown path → 404 response (`renderNotFound`-ish, html or JSON by Accept).
* Wrong method on a known path → Elysia 405 default.


# Streaming & SSE (/docs/http/streaming)



# Streaming & SSE [#streaming--sse]

## Server-side SSE [#server-side-sse]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/events.ts"
import { stream } from "@kwiva/http";

api.get("/stream", () => stream(async (controller) => {
  const promise = watchTodos((todo) => controller.enqueue(todo.toJSON()));
  controller.closed = () => { await promise; };
  return () => promise;
}, { heartbeatMs: 15_000, event: "todo" }));
```

## SSE payload format [#sse-payload-format]

`frame(id, event, data)` → `data: <json>\nid: <id>\nevent: <event>\n\n` (only if `event` provided); `controller.closed` on client disconnect.

## Client-side consumption [#client-side-consumption]

```ts title="src/app/ui/pages/events.tsx"
const response = await fetch("/api/events/stream");
const reader = response.body.getReader();
```

Or via `@kwiva/events` (see [Events → broadcast metadata](/docs/realtime/events)).

> \[!TIP]
> `controller.enqueue` is sync-or-async (yields are sent as soon as possible); `controller.close()` ends stream.


# Validation (/docs/http/validation)



# Validation [#validation]

## Route-level input [#route-level-input]

```ts title="src/app/http/controllers/posts.ts"
api.post("/", handler, {
  input: {
    params: "/api/posts/:id",
    query: { page: NumberSchema },
    body: CreatePostSchema,
    headers: HttpSchema,
    cookie: CookieSchema,
  },
});
```

## Validation pipeline [#validation-pipeline]

`validateInput(context, route, overrides?)` → `{params, query, body, headers?, cookies?}` — parsed+validated per section.

## `parsePart(part, schema, value)` [#parsepartpart-schema-value]

Throws `ValidationError{fields: Record<string, string[]>}` on failure.

## Error shape [#error-shape]

```json title="422"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION",
    "message": "Invalid input",
    "fields": { "body.title": ["Too short"] },
    "requestId": "req_abc123"
  }
}
```

## Custom validation middleware [#custom-validation-middleware]

```ts title="src/app/http/middleware/tenant.ts"
import { defineMiddleware } from "@kwiva/http";
import { abort } from "@kwiva/core";

export const TenantHeader = defineMiddleware((ctx, next) => {
  const tenant = ctx.headers().get("x-tenant");
  if (!tenant) throw abort("BAD_REQUEST", "Missing x-tenant header");
  return next(ctx);
});
```

## Contracts [#contracts]

`defineContract({request, response})` — merges request + response contracts (see [Controllers](/docs/http/controllers#contract)).


# WebSockets (/docs/http/websockets)



# WebSockets [#websockets]

## Channels [#channels]

```ts title="src/app/http/ws/channels.ts"
import { channel, broadcast, presence } from "@kwiva/http";

export const MessagesChannel = channel("messages").policy((user) => !!user);
export const OnlinePresence = presence("users:{id}").onJoin(...).onLeave(...).room("lobby");
```

## WS routes [#ws-routes]

```ts
export const ChatController = defineController({
  prefix: "/ws/chat",
  routes(api) {
    api.ws("/messages", {
      handler: async function* (ctx) {
        // yield per incoming message
        await handleIncoming(ctx.message);
      },
    });
  },
});
```

## Broadcasts [#broadcasts]

```ts title="src/app/http/ws/broadcast.ts"
export function broadcastNewTodo(todo) { broadcast("todo.new", todo); }
```

`broadcast(name, payload)` — hub-level; `topicCount(topic)`.

## Presence [#presence]

`Presence{pattern, onJoin, onLeave, room(key), join(key, user), leave(key, userId), members(key)}` — auto-leave on close.

## `AsyncQueue` [#asyncqueue]

`AsyncQueue<T>` — `push/take/close`.

## Event bridge (`@kwiva/events`) [#event-bridge-kwivaevents]

`broadcastEvent(event, data, overrides)` / `emitAndBroadcast` — maps `event.broadcastOn` → channel + `async fn` returning channel names.

## Client [#client]

* SSE fallback (`toSSEResponse` on client) — fetch loop
* `@kwiva/client` `useWsSubscription`

## Scaling [#scaling]

* In-process hub; single instance recommended for chat; multi-instance coordination requires adapter (external queue for ws).

> \[!TIP]
> `mountWsRoutes(app, routes, appCtx)` at boot; channels by name.


# What is Kwiva? (/docs)



## Overview [#overview]

Kwiva is the **batteries-included TypeScript application framework**. Instead of assembling a dozen unrelated libraries — a router here, a data layer there, a separate auth kit, a build tool, a generated client, and yet another admin UI — your application talks to one coherent framework: a framework-owned `@kwiva/*` API surface, a single configuration model, one CLI, and a Rust-speed toolchain for instant feedback.

You write plain TypeScript. App code imports only from `@kwiva/*` packages. Every construct you declare — a model, a controller, a page, a job, an event, a mail — is a `defineX` factory. Reading Kwiva app code should feel like reading a description of the product: models describe the data, controllers describe the HTTP surface, pages describe the UI, and the framework derives the rest.

### The problem it solves [#the-problem-it-solves]

A serious TypeScript application today usually means gluing unrelated libraries together. Each library ships its own conventions, its own configuration, its own failure modes, and its own upgrade cadence. Types stop at library boundaries. Configuration spreads across four formats. "Shipping" means re-learning integration details for every new element of the stack. The result is a fragile house of cards — a pile of parts that only coincidentally behaves like an application.

### The solution [#the-solution]

Kwiva collapses that stack into a single, coherent framework:

```plaintext title="the-solution.txt"
One project. One configuration model. One CLI. One defineX language.
```

* **Models** derive the entire data layer — database schema, migrations, seeders, REST API routes, the typed RPC client, OpenAPI, and MCP tools
* **Controllers** define HTTP endpoints with typed context, per-route validation, lifecycle hooks, and policy checks
* **Pages** render with streaming SSR, typed loaders, and full-stack type safety from database to browser
* **Auth, authorization, tenancy, queues, realtime, and observability** are built in, not bolted on

## Why Kwiva [#why-kwiva]

Kwiva is organized around four design pillars.

| Pillar                                      | What it means                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **One defineX grammar**                     | Every app construct is a `defineX` factory. Models are the single source of truth and derive the whole stack. Plain, serializable definitions — no decorators, no classes, no config sprawl.                              |
| **Developer experience**                    | CLI-first generators for everything, a typed config folder with sensible defaults, auto-discovery over manual registration, and friendly errors (did-you-mean suggestions, field-mapped validation, request correlation). |
| **Production-grade out of the box**         | Stateless by construction (externalized state), tenancy-first data access, queues and tasks for background scale, edge presets, and one codebase that deploys anywhere.                                                   |
| **Extensible without breaking the grammar** | The same grammar declares controllers, pages, jobs, policies, auth, storage, search, realtime — and engines stay sealed behind the framework, never imported by app code.                                                 |

## Architecture at a Glance [#architecture-at-a-glance]

Kwiva holds one core architectural rule:

```plaintext title="architecture-at-a-glance.txt"
Application (src/) — models, http, pages, jobs, events, config
  ↓  writes defineX(...) only · imports only @kwiva/*
Framework API surface (@kwiva/* — the packages)
  ↓
Sealed engines (framework-owned internals — never imported by app code)
  ↓
Runtime (Bun · Node · serverless · containers · edge) via presets
```

The application depends only on the framework. The framework owns the sealed engines and the Rust-speed toolchain. Whatever preset an application deploys to, it sees the same framework API surface; the differences between runtimes stay inside the engine layer.

### One Definition Multiplies the Stack [#one-definition-multiplies-the-stack]

A single model definition feeds an intermediate representation (the model IR) from which the rest of the stack is derived — so there is no drift between your types, your API, and your database:

```plaintext title="one-definition-multiplies-the-stack.txt"
src/app/models/*.ts ──► model IR
  ├─► database schema + migrations + seeders
  ├─► typed REST API routes (list / get / create / update / delete)
  ├─► typed RPC client SDK (@kwiva/client)
  ├─► OpenAPI 3.1 spec (/openapi.json)
  ├─► MCP tools (when opted in, policy-checked)
  └─► migrations, seeders, factories, verified by the test suite
```

## The defineX Ecosystem [#the-definex-ecosystem]

Every app-facing construct in Kwiva is a `defineX` factory — one consistent convention across the whole framework. Learn one, learn them all.

| Package          | Role                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@kwiva/core`    | Application kernel: `defineApp`, `defineConfig`, `loadConfig`, typed context/ALS, errors, `defineService`, model IR helpers, cache, KV, store contracts |
| `@kwiva/data`    | Models, field DSL, relations, query builder, transactions, migrations, seeders, factories, search ops                                                   |
| `@kwiva/http`    | Controllers, contracts, routes, middleware, server/pipeline, SSE/streams, WebSockets, OpenAPI, caching                                                  |
| `@kwiva/ui`      | Pages, layouts, routing, SSR/streaming/hydration, islands, navigation, SEO helpers, `./server`                                                          |
| `@kwiva/client`  | Typed RPC client (Eden + TanStack Query), reads/mutations/infinite/form/upload hooks, cache persistence, token refresh, WS                              |
| `@kwiva/auth`    | `defineAuth` providers, sessions, identity flows, policies/gates/abilities, controllers, middleware                                                     |
| `@kwiva/jobs`    | Jobs, queues, workers, middleware, unique jobs, outbox, priorities, failed-job registry, tasks, cron scheduler, observability                           |
| `@kwiva/events`  | Events, listeners, broadcast, subscribers, config, testing fakes                                                                                        |
| `@kwiva/mail`    | `defineMail`, templates (markdown + string + components), transports (memory/console/SMTP/Resend)                                                       |
| `@kwiva/mcp`     | MCP v2: config, tool generation (model + controller), custom tools, HTTP fetch + stdio server, auth                                                     |
| `@kwiva/storage` | Disks, storage API, uploads, signed URLs, assets, tenant scoping, fakes                                                                                 |
| `@kwiva/search`  | Config validation, Postgres FTS, federated search, `reindexSearch`                                                                                      |
| `@kwiva/testing` | `withApp`, `createTestClient`, shared boot seam, DB lifecycle helpers, fakes                                                                            |
| `@kwiva/cli`     | The `kwiva` binary, generators, migrations, db commands, app commands, platform commands                                                                |

Plus sealed engine packages (`@kwiva/auth-better-auth`, `@kwiva/jobs-pg-boss`, `@kwiva/mail-resend`, `@kwiva/mail-smtp`, `@kwiva/store-redis`) behind the framework API.

## What you get out of the box [#what-you-get-out-of-the-box]

* One model definition that derives: database schema + migrations + seeders, the REST API, the typed RPC client, OpenAPI, MCP tools, and audit trails
* Typed validation at every boundary (field DSL + Standard Schema + contracts), with field-mapped error shapes
* Built-in auth (sessions, providers, identity flows), authorization (policies, gates, abilities), and tenancy-first data access
* Streaming SSR with islands and typed navigation — not bolt-ons, but wired into pages
* Queues and jobs with middleware, retries, batches, and lifecycle observability
* A CLI that generates the whole tree: scaffolding, controllers, migrations, seeders, tests, routes
* A shared, typed config folder per environment with validation

## When to use Kwiva [#when-to-use-kwiva]

* Teams building one app on one codebase, full-stack or backend-heavy
* Products that need typed contracts, auth, tenancy, and background work without assembling a dozen libraries
* Products that want a boring, verifiable stack — types and database never drift apart

## When not to use Kwiva [#when-not-to-use-kwiva]

* Teams already happy with their assembled stack of libraries
* Projects that need a visual drag-drop CMS or hosted cloud experience (out of scope for the framework)
* Non-TypeScript applications

## FAQ [#faq]

### What is Kwiva's relationship with Bun? [#what-is-kwivas-relationship-with-bun]

Bun is the primary runtime (`engines: bun >= 1.4.0`) and the native execution environment for development — fast startup, isolated module loading, and a fast transpiler-based toolchain. It is a runtime choice, not a framework identity: Node and serverless/container targets stay compatible through presets, and the framework API surface is the same on every target.

### Is Kwiva a framework or a library? [#is-kwiva-a-framework-or-a-library]

A framework: it owns the application-facing surface, the lifecycle, and the conventions. Applications write `src/app/**` constructs with `defineX` factories and consume `@kwiva/*` — they never import an engine.

### Is the framework versioned? [#is-the-framework-versioned]

The docs mirror the current implementation: packages are at `@kwiva/*` `0.2.0`, tracking the `main` branch of the Kwiva framework repo (no git tags yet). See [Versioning & Compatibility](/reference/versioning).

### Studio, addons, and cloud [#studio-addons-and-cloud]

Not documented on this site — they are roadmap items on the framework side (see `docs/features/studio.md` in the framework repo). This site tracks the shipped product.

# Addons & Distribution (/docs/modules-plugins/addons)



An **addon** is any installable capability package: a **module** (a full-stack capability), a **plugin** (an HTTP-level extension), or a **theme** (a ui-kit skin). All three share one installation path — the addon workflow is the single way capabilities are installed and registered in a Kwiva app. This page covers that workflow end to end: what an addon is, how it installs, how it is discovered, how versions are resolved, and how you publish your own.

## What Is an Addon? [#what-is-an-addon]

The source of an addon does not change the workflow:

| Source      | Example                            | How it installs                       |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| First-party | `@kwiva/blog`                      | `kwiva add @kwiva/blog`               |
| Third-party | any addon tagged for the ecosystem | `kwiva add <addon>`                   |
| Local       | `./addons/analytics`               | `kwiva add ./addons/analytics --path` |

The kind of addon shapes what it contributes but not how it is managed. A module brings the full vertical stack — models, controllers, pages, jobs, config, and migrations. A plugin extends the HTTP surface — middleware, route rules, and lifecycle hooks. A theme restyles the ui-kit. All three install, list, update, and remove through the same commands.

## The Addon CLI [#the-addon-cli]

| Command                           | Purpose                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kwiva add <addon>`               | Install and register an addon — package, config entry, and migrations check |
| `kwiva add <addon> --path`        | Install a local addon from a workspace path                                 |
| `kwiva add <addon> --version <v>` | Pin a specific version                                                      |
| `kwiva addons list`               | Show installed addons: contributions and versions                           |
| `kwiva addons search <term>`      | Search the registry                                                         |
| `kwiva addons info <addon>`       | Show details of an addon before you commit                                  |
| `kwiva addons remove <addon>`     | Remove an installed addon, leaving its migrations intact and flagged        |
| `kwiva addons update [addon]`     | Update addons within their `requires` compatibility ranges                  |
| `kwiva addons outdated`           | List addons with newer compatible versions available                        |

The full command reference for this surface lives on [CLI Addon Commands](/docs/cli/addon-commands).

## Installing an Addon [#installing-an-addon]

One command installs, registers, and checks:

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva add @kwiva/blog
```

`kwiva add` does three things at once:

1. **Installs** the package from the registry.
2. **Registers** it — it writes the module entry into `kwiva.config.ts` for you.
3. **Checks migrations** — module migrations are validated so the addon's schema steps apply cleanly with the app's migrations, and anything needing `db:migrate` is flagged.

After `kwiva add`, the addon's contributions — models, controllers, pages, config, migrations — are live in the app, registered in configuration, and subject to the same conventions and gates as first-party code.

Local addons work identically with a path instead of a package name:

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva add ./addons/analytics --path
```

Pinning follows the same one-step shape:

```bash title="terminal"
kwiva add @kwiva/blogstore --version 2.1.0
```

Manual registration in `kwiva.config.ts` remains supported for vendored and path-based modules that were never installed through the CLI:

```ts title="kwiva.config.ts"
// kwiva.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  modules: [
    './modules/billing',  // vendored or path-based registration
  ],
})
```

## Registry and Distribution Conventions [#registry-and-distribution-conventions]

Publishing an addon is a small, explicit contract:

1. The package **exports the `defineModule` result** as its default export.
2. It is **tagged with the `kwiva-addon` keyword** in the package registry.
3. It declares **`requires` ranges** for its `@kwiva/*` peer dependencies.

With that contract in place:

* `kwiva add @acme/chat` installs and registers the module.
* `kwiva addons search chat` lists it — backed by a curated addon index.
* The app pins versions with semver; compatibility is enforced via `requires` ranges.

The keyword is the discovery bridge. `kwiva addons search` matches on it, and the curated addon index maintains quality and compatibility signals for what search returns. `kwiva addons info` is the pre-install look: description, contribution summary (which models, controllers, pages, or config the addon brings), requirements, and changelog.

## Version and Upgrade Management [#version-and-upgrade-management]

Kwiva resolves upgrades against declared compatibility rather than blindly bumping:

* `kwiva addons update` brings every addon to the newest version **within its `requires` range** — it refuses to jump outside a declared compatible window.
* `kwiva addons outdated` reports what is behind, so upgrades become deliberate decisions rather than periodic rituals.
* `kwiva addons info <addon>` shows the installed version, available versions, and requirements before you commit to a move.
* `kwiva addons remove <addon>` unregisters and removes the addon cleanly — the package is uninstalled and the registry entry removed, but any schema the addon contributed is left intact and flagged so database data is never silently dropped.

Because the app pins versions and addons declare `requires`, two apps can hold different addon versions without breakage — upgrades are deliberate, per-app decisions. When an addon's `requires` range conflicts with what the app already pins, resolution rejects the combination instead of running an incompatibility.

> \[!TIP]
> `kwiva addons outdated` plus `kwiva addons info` is the review loop for a low-risk upgrade: find what is behind, read the requirements and changelog, then `kwiva addons update <addon>` to move within the compatible range.

## First-Party Addons [#first-party-addons]

Framework-maintained addons cover the common platform capabilities:

| Addon                  | Ships                                                                 |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@kwiva/auth-kit`      | Ready auth screens (sign-in, sign-up, OAuth) + user-management polish |
| `@kwiva/blog`          | Posts, tags, and comments models + pages + feed                       |
| `@kwiva/billing`       | Plans, subscriptions, invoices + webhooks (engine-agnostic gateway)   |
| `@kwiva/notifications` | In-app + email notification stack                                     |
| `@kwiva/analytics`     | Event tracking + dashboards                                           |

These demonstrate the shape a well-built addon takes — namespaced contributions, config defaults apps can override, migrations ordered before app migrations, and `requires` ranges that keep them upgradable.

## Authoring and Publishing an Addon [#authoring-and-publishing-an-addon]

Everything else is publishable by anyone. The authoring surface is the same one you use in an application — `defineModule` for modules, `definePlugin` for plugins, and a ui-kit skin for themes:

1. **Scaffold** — `kwiva make:module analytics` creates the module folder with slots for each contribution type.
2. **Author** — declare contributions through `defineModule`; set namespaced config defaults; declare `requires`.
3. **Test locally** — register the module from its workspace path (`./addons/analytics`) in a real app and exercise what it contributes.
4. **Build** — `kwiva module:build` packages the module with its contribution manifest and a compiled distribution (bundled output plus isolated type declarations).
5. **Publish** — publish to the package registry tagged with the `kwiva-addon` keyword.

From then on, `kwiva add @acme/analytics` installs it into any compatible app, and `kwiva addons search analytics` makes it discoverable to everyone else.

## The Consumer–Author Contract [#the-consumerauthor-contract]

The contract holds in both directions:

* **Consumers** get a surface with no guessing — search, info, install, update, remove, and audit are all first-class commands.
* **Authors** get one publishing path — package with the keyword, and the addon becomes discoverable through the CLI rather than word of mouth.

That symmetry is what makes the addon model a distribution story rather than a set of copy-paste instructions.

* [Defining Modules](/docs/modules-plugins/defining-modules) — the contribution points an addon ships
* [Application Composition](/docs/modules-plugins/composition) — how registered modules join the kernel
* [Modules & Plugins](/docs/modules-plugins) — the composition model at a glance
* [CLI Addons](/docs/cli/addon-commands) — the command reference for addon workflows
* [Modules Reference](/docs/cli/generators) — generators that scaffold new modules


# Application Composition (/docs/modules-plugins/composition)



# Application Composition [#application-composition]

`defineApp(options)` — the app is the composition root:

```ts title="bootstrap/app.ts"
import { defineApp } from "@kwiva/core";
import { TodosModule } from "@app/modules/todos";

export default defineApp({
  name: "my-app",
  modules: [TodosModule],
  policies: [...], // additive
  state: { counter: 0 },
  resolve: [["api", () => apiClient()]],
});
```

## DefineApp options [#defineapp-options]

| Field                                                                                                          | Type                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`                                                                                                         | string (required)                                                |
| `models`, `controllers`, `middleware`, `services`, `policies`, `pages`, `jobs`, `events`, `commands`, `macros` | arrays (additive)                                                |
| `state`                                                                                                        | object (app state)                                               |
| `decorate`                                                                                                     | `(app) => AppContext`                                            |
| `resolve`                                                                                                      | `Array<[string, Resolver]>` — DI-like (n `[key, () => service]`) |
| `state`                                                                                                        | shared state                                                     |

## Discovery + assembly [#discovery--assembly]

`assembleApp(app, root)` — discovers units, merges additive, registers policies/pages.

## Shutdown [#shutdown]

`await server.stop()` — flush afterResponse, cancel workers, close DB.

> \[!TIP]
> For shutdown hooks, see [Observability](/docs/observability/dev-overlay) or app bootstrap.


# Defining Modules (/docs/modules-plugins/defining-modules)



# Defining Modules [#defining-modules]

```ts
import { defineModule } from "@kwiva/core";

export const TodosModule = defineModule({
  name: "todos",
  models: [Todo, Task],
  policies: [TodoPolicy],
  controllers: [TodosController],
  tasks: [CleanupTask],
});
```

## API [#api]

| Field                | Type    | Notes                   |
| -------------------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `name`               | string  | module name (namespace) |
| `models`             | `any[]` | models to include       |
| `controllers`        | `any[]` | HTTP controllers        |
| `policies` / `gates` | `any[]` | auth policies           |
| `jobs`               | `any[]` | jobs                    |
| `events`             | `any[]` | events                  |
| `services`           | `any[]` | services                |
| `tasks`              | `any[]` | tasks                   |
| `commands`           | `any[]` | app commands            |
| `middleware`         | `any[]` | http middleware         |

## Discovery [#discovery]

Modules are discovered from `src/app/**` (see [Auto-Discovery](/docs/core-concepts/auto-discovery)). Modules can also be passed explicitly via `defineApp({modules: [TodosModule, ...]})`.

> \[!TIP]
> For the "app code" pattern, see examples/todo-app-m4-m7.


# Modules & Plugins (/docs/modules-plugins)



# Modules & Plugins [#modules--plugins]

Kwiva composes apps from composable pieces:

1. **Factories** — `defineApp/Config/Service` (core), `defineModel` (data), `defineController` (http), etc.
2. **Modules** — `defineModule` — reusable packages (see [Defining Modules](/docs/modules-plugins/defining-modules))
3. **Plugins** — `definePlugin` — lifecycle-hoc pieces (see [Application Composition](/docs/modules-plugins/composition))
4. **Addons** — registry/search/publish system — **not implemented yet** (roadmap; per project decision we skip this area).

## Entry points [#entry-points]

| Topic                   | Page                                                       |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Defining Modules        | [Defining Modules](/docs/modules-plugins/defining-modules) |
| Application Composition | [Composition](/docs/modules-plugins/composition)           |


# Dev Overlay (/docs/observability/dev-overlay)



# Dev Overlay [#dev-overlay]

Available during `kwiva dev`: a live timeline of requests, spans, errors, DB queries, and cache activity.

## How to enable [#how-to-enable]

Set `DEBUG=1` or add `devOverlay` to `src/config/app.ts`:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  // @ts-expect-error dev-only
  devOverlay: true,
});
```

## Panels [#panels]

* Request timeline (HTTP + WS)
* Span waterfall
* Error list (located)
* DB query log
* Cache hit/miss

## Related [#related]

* [Logging](/docs/observability/logging)
* [Tracing](/docs/observability/tracing)
* [Metrics](/docs/observability/metrics)


# Observability (/docs/observability)



# Observability [#observability]

* **Logging** — [Logging](/docs/observability/logging)
* **Tracing** — [Tracing](/docs/observability/tracing)
* **Metrics** — [Metrics](/docs/observability/metrics)
* **Dev Overlay** — [Dev Overlay](/docs/observability/dev-overlay)

## TL;DR [#tldr]

Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs, OTel spans, job events, and a live dev overlay during `kwiva dev`.


# Logging (/docs/observability/logging)



# Logging [#logging]

## `@kwiva/core` logger [#kwivacore-logger]

```ts
import { getLogger } from "@kwiva/core";
const logger = getLogger("posts");
logger.info("todo.created", { id: 1, userId: 42 });
```

* Structured: `{level, message, timestamp, correlationId, data}`
* Default sink: JSON to stdout in prod
* Dev sink: pretty console in dev

## Correlation IDs [#correlation-ids]

Set `correlationId` on the logger; chained spans via `child(logger)`.

## Where used [#where-used]

* HTTP: `ctx.logger.info("request.done", { method, url })`
* Jobs: `JobContext.logger`
* Worker: `startWorker({logger})`

## Dev overlay [#dev-overlay]

`createLogger` + watch logs in terminal during `kwiva dev`.

## Export [#export]

Canonical OTel-style: `withTrace`, `span()` etc. — advanced, see tracing.

> \[!TIP]
> `bun:test` + logger = free observability for dev.


# Metrics (/docs/observability/metrics)



# Metrics [#metrics]

## `@kwiva/jobs` metrics [#kwivajobs-metrics]

`queueMetrics()` — from inventory.

## HTTP metrics [#http-metrics]

* Request counters by status (built-in middleware? — via `rateLimit`? no — via dev overlay)
* Durations via spans (tracing)

## Export [#export]

See research + `@kwiva/core` logger metrics module (m4-m5): `observability/metrics` — advanced.

> \[!TIP]
> See [Tracing](/docs/observability/tracing) + [Queue metrics](/docs/observability/observability).


# Tracing (/docs/observability/tracing)



# Tracing [#tracing]

## Spans [#spans]

Every handler execution creates a span tree:

```
[request] (correlation id)
├── [middleware]
│   └── [handler] → span
├── [db.query] (kysely)
```

## Exporters [#exporters]

* OpenTelemetry exporter (OTLP) — see research
* Console exporter (dev)

## `observe` API [#observe-api]

`createSpan`, `span`, `withTrace`.

> \[!TIP]
> Only after Phase J.


# Channels (/docs/realtime/channels)



# Channels [#channels]

```ts title="src/app/http/ws/channels.ts"
import { channel } from "@kwiva/http";

export const NotificationsChannel = channel("notifications.{userId}").policy((user) => !!user);
export const PresenceChannel = channel("presence.{room}");
```

## Policies [#policies]

`channel().policy(fn)` — policy-checked at subscribe time.

## Dynamic segments [#dynamic-segments]

`channel("notifications.{userId}")` — `subscribe("notifications.42")` passes `{userId: "42"}` to policy fn.

## Presence [#presence]

`presence("users.{id}")` — `onJoin`, `onLeave`, `members()`.

## Notes [#notes]

See also [broadcast metadata via Events](/docs/realtime/events).


# Client-Side Realtime (/docs/realtime/client-usage)



# Client-Side Realtime [#client-side-realtime]

`@kwiva/client` — WS hooks.

```tsx
import { useWsSubscription, useConnectionState } from "@kwiva/client";

const { data, error, status, send } = useWsSubscription("NotificationsChannel");
```

## `useConnectionState` — returns `{status}` where status is `"idle"|"active"|"error"`. [#useconnectionstate--returns-status-where-status-is-idleactiveerror]

## Subscriptions [#subscriptions]

`connectRoute(routeId, args, {reconnect?})` — returns `ManagedSocket{send, close, status}`.

## SSE fallback [#sse-fallback]

`toSSEResponse` — fetch loop with `readAsStream`.

## Status enum [#status-enum]

* WS: `idle | active | error | completed`
* Connections: `idle | connecting | connected | disconnected`

> \[!TIP]
> With @kwiva/events, see [Events & Broadcasting](/docs/realtime/events).


# Events & Broadcasting (/docs/realtime/events)



# Events & Broadcasting [#events--broadcasting]

```ts title="src/app/events/todo-created.ts"
import { defineEvent } from "@kwiva/events";

export const TodoCreated = defineEvent<{ id: string; title: string }>({
  broadcastOn: { module: "todos" },
  broadcastAs: "todos.created",
  broadcastWith: (data) => ({ id: data.id, title: data.title }),
  broadcastWhen: (data) => !!data.id,
});
```

## Listener [#listener]

```ts title="src/app/listeners/notify-team.ts"
import { defineListener } from "@kwiva/events";
import { TodoCreated } from "@kwiva/events";

export const NotifyTeamListener = defineListener({
  on: TodoCreated,
  queue: { tries: 3, backoffMs: 1000 },
  shouldHandle(data) { return data.title !== "internal"; },
  handle: async (data) => { /* audit, notify */ },
});
```

## Broadcast → channels [#broadcast--channels]

`channelFor(data)` — maps `broadcastOn` to channel names.

## Transactional outbox [#transactional-outbox]

`enqueueOutbox(TodoCreated, data)` — dispatched via `drainOutbox()`.


# Realtime (/docs/realtime)



# Realtime [#realtime]

* **Events**: [Events & Broadcasting](/docs/realtime/events)
* **Channels**: [Channels](/docs/realtime/channels)
* **Client-side**: [Client-Side Realtime](/docs/realtime/client-usage)
* **Scaling**: [Scaling Realtime](/docs/realtime/scaling)

## Architecture [#architecture]

```
emitEvent → listener (sync/queued) → broadcast → channel → client hooks
```


# Scaling Realtime (/docs/realtime/scaling)



# Scaling Realtime [#scaling-realtime]

## Single instance (recommended) [#single-instance-recommended]

Simple hub in `@kwiva/http` — `broadcast`, `subscribe`, `topicCount`, `resetHub`.

## Multi-instance [#multi-instance]

Requires: external broker or partitioned queues for broadcast; coordination via `presence` maps; zero-downtime redeploys via WS close codes.

> \[!TIP]
> For chat, in-process hub suffices. For global notifications, use DB outbox + polling loop as fallback.


# Compatibility Matrix (/docs/reference/compatibility)



# Compatibility [#compatibility]

## Bun [#bun]

`>= 1.4.0` — required for `import.meta.main`, Bun.serve, etc.

## Node [#node]

`>= 20` — API-only, supported via engines.

## Databases [#databases]

* Postgres ≥ 12 — all apps require for Postgres configs
* PGlite — dev/test only

## Transports [#transports]

| Package        | Transport                           |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `mail-smtp`    | SMTP (Nodemailer), `pool` supported |
| `mail-resend`  | Resend API                          |
| `jobs-pg-boss` | pg-boss (durable)                   |
| `store-redis`  | ioredis (REDIS\_URL)                |

# Troubleshooting (/docs/reference/troubleshooting)



# Troubleshooting [#troubleshooting]

## `bun install` fails [#bun-install-fails]

* Check `engines.bun` — update Bun first.

## `kwiva dev` won't start [#kwiva-dev-wont-start]

* Run `kwiva doctor` — checks storage/search/mcp
* Check `src/config` for invalid sections (`bunx tsc --noEmit`)

## `kwiva migrate` errors [#kwiva-migrate-errors]

* Run `kwiva migrate:status` first
* Look for timestamped names, `.d.ts`

## DB not found [#db-not-found]

* `dataDir` for pglite; `database` config via `kwiva dev`

## Test hangs [#test-hangs]

* `setupTestDb` + `teardownTestDb` in beforeEach/afterEach

> \[!TIP]
> For deeper issues, see [observability/dev-overlay](/docs/observability/dev-overlay).

# Caching Strategies (/docs/rendering/caching)



# Caching Strategies [#caching-strategies]

| Layer        | Where                                   | Details                                 |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Route rules  | `ctx.response.set({cache: {ttl, swr}})` | —                                       |
| Model cache  | core `Cache` (Keyv)                     | `getCache/initCache`                    |
| Client cache | TanStack Query                          | [Data Hooks](/docs/frontend/data-hooks) |
| CDN          | —                                       | via route rules + public mode           |

## invalidation [#invalidation]

`cache.invalidateTags([...])` — invalidates by tag (model: `invalidateModel` helper).


# Hydration (/docs/rendering/hydration)



# Hydration [#hydration]

## `hydrateApp(options)` → `unmount()` [#hydrateappoptions--unmount]

Reads `window.__KWIVA__`, hydrates via `hydrateRoot`.

## `usePage`/`useRouter` — client router. [#usepageuserouter--client-router]

## `renderPageState(state, pages, layouts)` [#renderpagestatestate-pages-layouts]

Reconstructs the same route tree on the client.

## Asset transfer [#asset-transfer]

`assetUrl`, `assetTags`, `parseAssetManifest` — compiled assets from manifest.


# Rendering (/docs/rendering)



# Rendering [#rendering]

Kwiva-owned SSR orchestrator (since Kwiva core owns rendering).

## Entry points [#entry-points]

| Topic                         | Page                                              |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| SSR (Server-Side Rendering)   | [Server-Side Rendering](/docs/rendering/ssr)      |
| Streaming SSR                 | [Streaming SSR](/docs/rendering/streaming)        |
| Hydration                     | [Hydration](/docs/rendering/hydration)            |
| Caching strategies            | [Caching Strategies](/docs/rendering/caching)     |
| Static Generation (prerender) | [Static Generation](/docs/rendering/prerendering) |

## Pipeline [#pipeline]

```
GET /page
├── resolveRoute(pathname)
├── layout(resolveLayouts) → [root, ...nested]
├── page.load(ctx) → props (SSR-only)
├── layouts.render(props, ctx) → tree
└── document.render → Response
```

## Notes [#notes]

* No Vite plugin — Kwiva ships `buildClientBundle` + `bunx tsc` build (ADR-0008 era).
* Islands hydrate per `data-kwiva-hydrate` attribute.
* Streaming SSR with Suspense (`streamPage`).


# Static Generation (/docs/rendering/prerendering)



# Static Generation [#static-generation]

`prerender()` — crawl from sitemap or explicit list at build time.

## ISR [#isr]

Route rules with TTL.

## SPA fallback [#spa-fallback]

Supported for HTML routes.

> \[!TIP]
> `kwiva build` + `renderPage` + `assetUrl` — combined with `streamPage` for streaming pages.


# Server-Side Rendering (/docs/rendering/ssr)



# SSR [#ssr]

## `renderPage(page, ctx, options?)` [#renderpagepage-ctx-options]

`Response` — for `Accept: application/json` → `{component, url, props}` envelope.

## `streamPage(options)` [#streampageoptions]

Streaming document variant.

## Hydration [#hydration]

`hydrateApp(options)` — reads `window.__KWIVA__`, hydrates via `hydrateRoot`.

## Errors [#errors]

`redirect(path, status?)`, `notFound()` in `renderPage`.

## Document [#document]

`renderDocument({head, body, seed, clientScript})`; `AssetManifest{entry, files, css}` + `assetTags`.


# Streaming SSR (/docs/rendering/streaming)



# Streaming SSR [#streaming-ssr]

## Suspense [#suspense]

Plain React Suspense (`<Suspense>`).

## `stream()` (core, `@kwiva/http`) [#stream-core-kwivahttp]

```ts
export const response = stream(async (controller) => {
  controller.enqueue(<Suspense>{promise}</Suspense>); // via fetchPage
});
```

## Client consumption [#client-consumption]

Fetch + `readAsStream` — or use `@kwiva/http` `toSSEResponse`.

> \[!TIP]
> Also see [HTTP Streaming & SSE](/docs/http/streaming).


# Architecture Inventory (/docs/research/architecture-inventory)



# Architecture Inventory [#architecture-inventory]

**Generated from:** read-only traversal of the Kwiva framework repo (`kwivajs`) at commit `552115f` ("chore(release): version packages for the 0.2.0 release candidate", 2026-11-18) and the docs repo (`quiva-docs`) at its working state. Snapshot, not live data.

***

## 1. Kwiva repo layout [#1-kwiva-repo-layout]

```
kwivajs/
├── packages/                  # 20 @kwiva/* packages (all published, public)
│   ├── core/                  # @kwiva/core 0.2.0  — kernel, config, context, errors, logger, model IR, cache, kv, store
│   ├── data/                  # @kwiva/data 0.2.0  — models, query, migrations, seeders, factories, search, db runtime
│   ├── http/                  # @kwiva/http 0.2.0  — controllers, contracts, middleware, pipeline, server, openapi, websocket, stream
│   ├── ui/                    # @kwiva/ui 0.2.0    — pages, routing, SSR, islands, navigation, SEO, ./server
│   ├── client/                # @kwiva/client 0.2.0 — typed RPC, reads/mutations/upload hooks, cache, token refresh, WS
│   ├── auth/                  # @kwiva/auth 0.2.0  — defineAuth, providers, sessions, identity, policies, gates, client hooks
│   ├── jobs/                  # @kwiva/jobs 0.2.0  — defineJob/Task, dispatch, workers, middleware, scheduler, outbox, failed, metrics
│   ├── events/                # @kwiva/events 0.2.0 — defineEvent, listeners, subscribers, broadcast, config, fakes
│   ├── mail/                  # @kwiva/mail 0.2.0  — defineMail, templates, transports (smtp, resend), config
│   ├── mcp/                   # @kwiva/mcp 0.1.0   — MCP v2, config, tools, ./server (handler, stdio)
│   ├── search/                # @kwiva/search 0.1.0 — config validation, federated search, reindex
│   ├── storage/               # @kwiva/storage 0.1.0 — files-sdk disks, uploads, signed URLs, assets, fakes
│   ├── testing/               # @kwiva/testing 0.1.0 — withApp, createTestClient, ./boot, db lifecycle
│   ├── cli/                   # @kwiva/cli 0.3.0   — kwiva binary, 20 commands, 19 make kinds, codegen
│   ├── auth-better-auth/      # @kwiva/auth-better-auth 0.0.1 — sealed Better Auth adapter
│   ├── jobs-pg-boss/          # @kwiva/jobs-pg-boss 0.0.1 — pg-boss queue transport
│   ├── mail-smtp/             # @kwiva/mail-smtp 0.0.1 — nodemailer transport
│   ├── mail-resend/           # @kwiva/mail-resend 0.0.1 — Resend API transport
│   └── store-redis/           # @kwiva/store-redis 0.0.1 — Redis StoreDriver adapter
├── examples/                  # reference apps: todo-app-m2, todo-app-m3, todo-app-m4-m7
├── docs/
│   ├── framework/             # spec docset (v0.3, 21 ADRs) — has mirror + deviations drift over time
│   ├── features/, plans/, phases/, research/ ...
├── test/functionality/        # engine-import, barrel-surface, size-budget, folder-convention, graph gates
├── scripts/                   # workspace runner, ci-validate
├── build.ts                   # shared tsc build for all packages
└── bun.lock, package.json (workspaces: packages/*, examples/*)
```

**Build:** every package builds with `tsc` to `dist/` (`build.ts`), `exports` map uses `bun` condition → `src/*.ts` (monorepo dev), `types`/`import` → `dist/*.d.ts`/`dist/*.js` (published).

**Root:** private workspace (`0.0.0`), `engines.bun >= 1.4.0`, `type: "module"`, CI pipeline: `typecheck` → `test` → `build` → functionality gates; moon config parked (pre-1.0 schema, not active); changesets for versioning.

**Dev conventions:** engines sealed — `no-engine-imports` lint gate; code linted with oxlint (Rust-speed) via root and per-package scripts.

***

## 2. Kwiva package map (roles) [#2-kwiva-package-map-roles]

| Package                                   | One-line role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@kwiva/core`                             | Application kernel: `defineApp`, `defineConfig`, config sections (`app`, `logger`, `cache`, `kv`), context/ALS (request, auth, batch, tenant, transaction, afterResponse), errors (8-code taxonomy), logger, model IR (frozen), cache (`initCache`), KV (`initKv`), store contracts, helpers/collection barrels.                                                                   |
| `@kwiva/data`                             | Models: `defineModel`, field DSL (string/enum/dateTime/belongsTo/hasMany/...), query builder, relations (incl. morph, through), transactions, migrations/seeders/factories, runtime (`db`, `transaction`), REST restRoutes helpers, Postgres FTS (`.search()` etc.), `./testing`.                                                                                                  |
| `@kwiva/http`                             | HTTP: `defineController`, `defineContract`, `defineMiddleware`, route builder (`api.get/post/ws/group`), guards, macros, middleware stack (`cors`, `csrf`, `rateLimit` built-in), server/boot/mount/dispatch/rest, OpenAPI mount (Scalar, model schemas), SSE/stream, WebSocket routes + channels + presence + broadcastEvent, error mapping (8-code → HTTP status, field-mapped). |
| `@kwiva/ui`                               | Frontend: `definePage`, layouts, recursive page discovery, `./server` renderPage (SSR, streaming, islands, assets, hydration, SEO helpers), navigation (typed routes, Link, scroll restoration), router.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `@kwiva/client`                           | Typed client:eden adapter, routes typed, query hooks (`useResource`, `useList`, `useMutation`, `useUpload`, `useInfiniteList`, `useForm`, `connectRoute`), optimistic mutations, cache persistence, token refresh, SSR client, `./boot` not included here (that's testing).                                                                                                        |
| `@kwiva/auth`                             | Auth: `defineAuth` (providers: emailPassword, magicLink, oauth), sessions (memory store), identity (password reset, email verify, TOTP, API tokens, PKCE OAuth), middleware (`requireAuth`, `apiTokenAuth`, `passwordConfirmation`), controllers, policies/gates/abilities (`definePolicy`, `defineGate`, `authorize`, `authorizeGate`, `can/whereCan`).                           |
| `@kwiva/jobs`                             | Jobs: `defineJob` (retries, backoff, middleware, outbox, priority), `defineTask`, cron scheduler (`parseCron`), workers (`startWorker`), dispatch (`dispatch`, `dispatchBatch`, `dispatchChain`, `dispatchAfterResponse`), failed-job registry (`retryFailed`), events, metrics, outbox store.                                                                                     |
| `@kwiva/events`                           | Events: `defineEvent` (sync/queued, broadcast metadata, channelFor), listeners (`defineListener` with queue options), subscribers (`defineSubscriber`), config, fakes (`fakeEvents`).                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `@kwiva/mail`                             | Mail: `defineMail`, templates (markdown + string + components), transports (memory, console, smtp, resend), config, `validateMailConfig`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `@kwiva/mcp`                              | MCP: config (`validateMcpConfig`), tool generation (model + controller tools), custom tools (`defineMcpTool`, `registerMcpTool`), server handler (`createMcpServerHandler`), stdio server (`runStdio`), in-process client tests, rate limiting, audit.                                                                                                                             |
| `@kwiva/search`                           | Search: `validateSearchConfig`, Postgres FTS, federated `searchAcross`, reindex via `kwiva search:reindex`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `@kwiva/storage`                          | Storage: `Disk` + `Storage` classes, files-sdk adapters (local/memory/s3/gcs/azure/vercel-blob), signed URLs, assets manifest, fakes, errors (`StorageError`, 5 codes).                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `@kwiva/testing`                          | Testing: `withApp`, `createTestClient`, `bootAppFromRoot`, `./boot`, DB lifecycle (`setupTestDb` etc.), re-exports.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `@kwiva/cli`                              | CLI: `kwiva` bin, dev/build/test/create, app commands (`defineCommand`), generators (`make:*`, 19 kinds), platform commands, codegen (route-tree, page bundle, layout scan).                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `@kwiva/auth-better-auth`                 | Auth engine: `defineBetterAuth` + `mountBetterAuth` (engine not exposed publicly).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `@kwiva/jobs-pg-boss`                     | Job transport: `definePgBossQueue` — engine adapter with local pending mirror.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `@kwiva/mail-smtp` / `@kwiva/mail-resend` | Mail transports.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `@kwiva/store-redis`                      | StoreDriver adapter (redis via ioredis), `installRedisStore`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

***

## 3. Dependency graph (package → runtime deps) [#3-dependency-graph-package--runtime-deps]

Derived from `package.json` files in the repo.

```
@kwiva/core
├── @keyv/sqlite, keyv, evlog            (store, logger, errors/misc)
│   (peers: @keyv/postgres, @keyv/redis; dev: both)
@kwiva/data
└── @kwiva/core, kysely, pluralize       (+ dev: @electric-sql/pglite)
@kwiva/http
└── @kwiva/core, @kwiva/data, @kwiva/events, elysia, valibot,
    @elysia/openapi, @valibot/to-json-schema, @scalar/types
@kwiva/ui
└── @kwiva/core, @kwiva/http, devalue    (peers: react, react-dom)
@kwiva/client
└── @elysia/eden, @kwiva/core, @kwiva/http, @tanstack/react-query,
    @tanstack/query-persist-client-core   (peers: react, react-dom)
@kwiva/auth
└── @kwiva/core, @kwiva/http             (peers: react, react-dom)
@kwiva/jobs
└── @kwiva/core, croner                  (+ peeks: none)
@kwiva/events, @kwiva/search, @kwiva/mcp, @kwiva/testing
└── @kwiva/core (+ @kwiva/data/@kwiva/http/@kwiva/auth/@kwiva/ui/@kwiva/jobs for testing)
@kwiva/mail
└── @kwiva/core, marked
@kwiva/storage
└── @kwiva/core, files-sdk
    (peers: @aws-sdk/*, @azure/storage-blob, @google-cloud/storage, @vercel/blob)
@kwiva/testing
└── all others (auth, client, data, events, http, jobs, mail, ui)
@kwiva/cli
└── all framework packages, @clack/*, change-case, leven
    (+ engine transports: @kwiva/jobs-pg-boss, @kwiva/mail-smtp)
    + driver packages: @kwiva/store-redis, @kwiva/auth-better-auth(via mcp? no — auth engine, CLI references via devDeps? actually it's a separate package)
```

**Key boundary note:** engines are NOT in the public dependency graph — `elysia`, `better-auth`, `tanstack`, `kysely`, `pglite`, `evlog` etc. live in package deps; app code imports only `@kwiva/*`.

***

## 4. Boundary rules (non-negotiable, enforceable by lint) [#4-boundary-rules-non-negotiable-enforceable-by-lint]

* **No engine imports in app code** (`no-engine-imports` lint gate — oxlint; ADR-0009).
* App code imports only `@kwiva/*` (ADR-0009).
* Package graph is acyclic (`test/functionality/engine-imports.test.ts`, graph tests).
* Stateless by construction: externalized state via public config sections; multi-instance safe.
* Jobs go through `@kwiva/jobs` queue (in-memory default, outbox for durable).

***

## 5. Examples (reference apps) [#5-examples-reference-apps]

| App                      | Packages                                  | Key files                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `todo-app-m2` (0.0.3)    | core, data                                | `src/app/models/todo.ts`, `src/bootstrap/app.ts`, `src/config/{app,database}.ts`, `src/database/migrations/*`, `todo.test.ts`                                                                |
| `todo-app-m3` (0.0.3)    | core, data, events, http, mail            | `src/app/controllers/todo.ts`, `src/app/contracts/todos.ts`, `src/app/events/todo-created.ts`, `src/app/mail/todo-mail.ts`, Scalar OpenAPI docs mount                                        |
| `todo-app-m4-m7` (0.0.3) | all + cli, ui, auth, client, jobs, events | `src/bootstrap/{app,server}.ts`, `src/app/{auth,policies,jobs,tasks,events,mail,models,http}/*`, `src/ui/{pages,layouts}/*`, `src/.kwiva/types/route-tree.gen.ts`, tests in `test/*.test.ts` |


# Documentation Coverage Matrix (/docs/research/coverage-matrix)



# Documentation Coverage Matrix [#documentation-coverage-matrix]

**Audit:** Parts I–IX (from the MASTER PROMPT — Kwiva-specific adaptation) vs every page on quiva-docs (`content/docs`, `content/guides`, `content/architecture`, `content/api`, `content/blog`, `src/pages/*`).

Key (MASTER PROMPT §2, Master §1, and audit consistency): **Implemented** = verified in Kwiva source; **Internal** = exists but not public API; **Experimental** = public API but marked unstable/experimental; **Planned** = in Kwiva roadmap (Studio/addons/cloud — skipped per user decision); **Not documented** = MASTER wants docs, quiva-docs has nothing covering it (gaps to fix).

* **Removed/renamed pages:** `api/react.mdx` + `api/router.mdx` → `api/ui.mdx`; `api/queue.mdx` → `api/jobs.mdx`; `api/config.mdx` + `api/services.mdx` → `api/core.mdx` (folded).

| `@kwiva/testing`          | `@kwiva/auth, @kwiva/client, @kwiva/core, @kwiva/data, @kwiva/events, @kwiva/http, @kwiva/jobs, @kwiva/mail, @kwiva/ui`                                                                                                             | —                                                                                                                                                    | `oxlint, typescript`                                                                                             |
| `@kwiva/ui`               | `@kwiva/core, @kwiva/http, devalue`                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `react, react-dom`                                                                                                                                   | `@types/react, @types/react-dom, happy-dom, oxlint, react, react-dom, typescript`                                |

**Root (`kwiva` workspace root)**: `type: "module"`, `private`, `engines: bun >= 1.4.0`; tooling: `@changesets/cli, @moonrepo/cli (parked, pre-1.0), @types/bun, husky, lint-staged, prettier, typescript`, and per-package `oxlint` + `tsc` via the shared `build.ts`.

**No engine-import rule:** `test/functionality/engine-imports.test.ts` + oxlint `no-engine-imports` gate apps from importing `elysia`, `better-auth`, `tanstack`, `kysely`, `pglite`, etc. — engines live in package deps only.

**Internal graph:** `http → {core, data, events}`; `ui → {core, http}`; `client → {core, http}`; `auth → {core, http}`; `jobs → core`; `events → core`; `mail → core`; `mcp → {auth, core, data, http}`; `search → {core, data}`; `storage → core`; `testing → {auth, client, core, data, events, http, jobs, mail, ui}`; `cli → {everything}`; `auth-better-auth → {better-auth, @kwiva/auth? no — core, data, http}`; `jobs-pg-boss → jobs`; `mail-smtp → mail`; `mail-resend → mail`; `store-redis → core`.

"Gap" = quiva-docs statement is wrong, missing, or incomplete relative to reality. "Aging" = TRUE but would soon drift.
